# lowob research: article summaries

> One-paragraph summary of every lowob research article, newest first. Full text: https://lowob.com/llms-full.txt

## [Account Planning for the Top Twenty](https://lowob.com/research/account-planning-for-the-top-twenty/)

Published 2026-11-17. Account planning for the top twenty is the discipline of choosing the twenty or so customers with the most room to grow, writing a short plan for each, and reviewing those plans monthly with the people who serve the account. The evidence says most firms get the selection wrong and the cadence wrong. Gartner found customers chosen as key accounts mainly for their large spend were 51% less likely to increase it, and that organisations which update plans frequently and use them in customer decisions are three times more likely to build the customer's decision confidence. Pick by potential, keep the plan to a page, and review it every month.

## [Agentic AI vs Generative AI: What Changes When the Model Can Act](https://lowob.com/research/agentic-ai-vs-generative-ai/)

Published 2026-11-17. Generative AI is a model that produces content, such as text, images or code, in response to a prompt, and hands it to a person. Agentic AI uses the same kind of model inside a loop that plans steps, calls tools and acts in other systems to reach a goal. The model is often identical; the permissions are not. Once a model can act, the question becomes what it may change and who approves it.

## [AI Agent vs Chatbot: The Difference That Matters to a Buyer](https://lowob.com/research/ai-agent-vs-chatbot/)

Published 2026-11-17. A chatbot is a conversational interface that answers a person's questions, from a script or a language model. An AI agent is given a goal and works toward it, choosing its next step and acting through tools such as a CRM, a billing system or email. For a buyer, the useful question is what the system is allowed to change, because that sets the risk, the controls and the price.

## [AI Agents in Commercial Operations: The RevOps Tasks Worth Handing Over](https://lowob.com/research/ai-agents-in-commercial-operations/)

Published 2026-11-17. Commercial operations is where agents can do the most on their own and where two tasks must never leave a person. Seven of the twelve operations tasks in the **lowob** Agent Task Directory are rated level 3, act and report: record clean-up, enrichment, the pipeline pack, delivery reconciliation, outcome write-back, commission calculation and agent monitoring. Three stay as drafts, and two, maintaining shared definitions and granting system access, stay with a named person. Operations is also the function that builds the brain the other agents depend on, so start with the monitoring that keeps every other agent honest.

## [AI Agents in Customer Success and Account Management](https://lowob.com/research/ai-agents-in-customer-success-and-account-management/)

Published 2026-11-17. Customer success is the function where AI agents touch revenue a company already has. That makes the internal tasks very attractive and the customer-facing ones expensive to get wrong. Of the nine customer success and account management tasks in the **lowob** directory, five are rated high reliability: renewal briefs, ticket summaries, adviser reminders, scheduling and review decks, all of them prepared for a person. Answering and resolving customer questions can run with an approved knowledge base, an escalation path and sampling, but a tribunal has already held a company liable for its chatbot's wrong answer. Start inside the account team, and earn the customer-facing tasks with measured evidence.

## [AI Agents in Marketing: What They Can Do Now, Task by Task](https://lowob.com/research/ai-agents-in-marketing-what-they-can-do-now/)

Published 2026-11-17. Marketing has more tasks rated High reliability than any other function in the **lowob** Agent Task Directory, and fewer that should run alone. Agents monitor competitors, draft campaign variants, write content briefs and assemble monthly reports well. The limits come from where marketing output goes: to the public, to regulators and to the budget. Of thirteen tasks, three can act and report, three can act with approval and seven stay as drafts, including publishing and budget moves. Start with monitoring, interview-to-draft content and the monthly report.

## [AI Agents in Partners and Distribution: What Works and What Leaks](https://lowob.com/research/ai-agents-in-partners-and-distribution/)

Published 2026-11-17. Partner and distribution work is a good place for AI agents to draft and monitor, and a poor place for them to decide. Of the nine partner tasks in the **lowob** directory, five are rated high reliability, and every one of those is internal drafting or monitoring. The tasks that settle who gets credit, which partner owns a deal, or what terms are on offer depend on rules that most partner programmes have never written down. An agent cannot apply a rule that does not exist. Start with marketplace monitoring, enablement packs and quarterly review preparation, and write the rules of engagement before you automate attribution or conflict.

## [AI Agents in Sales: What They Can Do Now, Task by Task](https://lowob.com/research/ai-agents-in-sales-what-they-can-do-now/)

Published 2026-11-17. Of the seventeen sales tasks in the **lowob** Agent Task Directory, three can run and report today, three can act with a seller's approval, ten should stay as drafts and one, approving a discount, should never leave a person. Agents are reliable on internal work a seller can check in a minute: call summaries, stale-deal flags, source tags and meeting briefs. They are weak wherever a task reaches a prospect, commits money or shapes the forecast. Start with the first group and move one task up the dial at a time, on evidence.

## [AI Copilot vs AI Agent: What Is the Difference?](https://lowob.com/research/ai-copilot-vs-ai-agent/)

Published 2026-11-17. An AI copilot assists a person who stays in control of every step: it answers questions, drafts text and summarises, and the person decides what happens next. An AI agent is given a goal and works toward it in a loop, choosing its own next step and acting through tools within set limits. The practical difference is how far up the autonomy dial the system sits, and who is accountable when it acts.

## [Build vs Buy AI Agents: A Decision Guide for Mid-Size Firms](https://lowob.com/research/build-vs-buy-ai-agents/)

Published 2026-11-17. Buying an AI agent means paying a vendor for a packaged product that does a defined job. Building one means assembling models, tools and orchestration code yourself. For most firms of 20 to 500 people the answer is to buy or configure the agent, and to own the part no vendor can supply: the record of what was decided, by whom, and what happened next.

## [Building a Community That Lasts: The Complete Guide](https://lowob.com/research/building-a-community-that-lasts/)

Published 2026-11-17. A community that lasts is a group of people doing a job together, with a reason to return that does not depend on being paid. Most company communities fail one of three tests: they are audiences rather than groups whose members create value for each other, they were recruited with incentives that selected for people who leave, or they are measured by member count, which says little about either. This guide sets out the sequence **lowob** recommends, from naming what you have to measuring who is still there after the incentives stop, and points to the article that covers each stage in depth.

## [Building the Commercial System at 20, 50 and 200 People](https://lowob.com/research/building-the-commercial-system-at-every-size/)

Published 2026-11-17. The commercial system is the same set of decisions at every size: who to sell to, how to reach them, what to charge, what to forecast and how to learn from the result. What changes is the problem it has to solve. At around 20 people, the system lives in the founders' heads and the job is to write it down. At around 50, the same words start to mean different things in different teams, and the job is shared definitions with owners. At around 200, managers make most decisions, and the job is reasoning that travels without its author. Build for the next size, not two sizes up.

## [Campaign Testing That Reaches a Decision](https://lowob.com/research/campaign-testing-that-reaches-a-decision/)

Published 2026-11-17. A campaign test reaches a decision when three things are fixed before it starts: the metric, the smallest effect worth acting on, and what the firm will do for each possible result. Most B2B tests skip all three and are too small to detect anything. Detecting a lift in landing page conversion from 3% to 3.6% needs about 14,000 visitors in each arm; Forrester finds fewer than 1% of leads become closed deals, so testing on revenue directly is rarely possible. The workable approach is to test bigger changes on upstream metrics, use concurrent holdouts rather than before-and-after comparisons, and record every result, including the null ones.

## [Channel Conflict, and How to Manage It](https://lowob.com/research/channel-conflict-and-how-to-manage-it/)

Published 2026-11-17. Channel conflict happens when two routes to the same customer compete for the same deal: a direct seller and a reseller, two partners, or a marketplace listing and a partner quote. It cannot be removed, because most B2B technology still reaches buyers through partners and the direct team will always meet them in the same accounts. It can be kept small. The evidence suggests that how often conflict happens matters more than how bad any one dispute gets, so the aim is fewer disputes, settled fast, under rules written down before the first one arrives. Every ruling should be recorded with its reason, because the rulings are what improve the rules.

## [Co-Selling With Platforms](https://lowob.com/research/co-selling-with-platforms/)

Published 2026-11-17. Co-selling is a structured arrangement in which a vendor and a platform's sales team work the same customer opportunity: the vendor shares deals with the platform, the platform's account team supports them, and, once the vendor has earned it, the platform refers opportunities back. The large cloud programmes, including AWS's ACE programme and Microsoft's partner programme, provide the mechanics. Whether they produce anything depends on one question: does your product grow the platform's own number? Platform sellers are measured on their platform's revenue, consumption and customer outcomes, and they spend time on partners that move those. A vendor that cannot show how it does will share pipeline and receive little back.

## [Commercial KPIs a Board Will Trust](https://lowob.com/research/commercial-kpis-a-board-will-trust/)

Published 2026-11-17. A board trusts a commercial KPI when it has one written definition, reconciles to a number finance already reports, keeps the same meaning from quarter to quarter, and has a named owner who can explain a movement. Most commercial packs fail at least one of those tests. Gartner found only 45% of sales leaders and sellers have high confidence in their organisation's forecasting accuracy, and only 47% believe their organisation has high-quality data. The fix is not more metrics. It is fewer, defined once, with every change of definition recorded like any other commercial decision.

## [Content With a Job](https://lowob.com/research/content-with-a-job/)

Published 2026-11-17. A piece of B2B content has a job when you can name its reader, the decision it helps that reader make, the stage of the purchase it serves and the action that should follow. Most libraries fail that test: Forrester found sales reps choosing from an average of 1,400 assets, and Gartner found 69% of buyers report inconsistencies between a supplier's website and what its sellers tell them. Two shifts make the job more specific than it used to be. Search sends fewer clicks, so content must be the source an answer cites; and buying groups average about 13 people, so content must help one buyer make the case to the rest.

## [CRM vs CDP vs Data Warehouse: Which Holds What](https://lowob.com/research/crm-vs-cdp-vs-data-warehouse/)

Published 2026-11-17. A CRM (customer relationship management system) is where a commercial team works: contacts, accounts, interactions and the deal pipeline, mostly entered by people. A customer data platform (CDP) collects customer data from many sources, links it into one profile per customer and shares those profiles with other tools, mainly for marketing. A data warehouse holds current and historical data from all of these systems for analysis and reporting. Most firms of 20 to 500 people need a CRM, many need a warehouse, and fewer need a CDP.

## [Demand Generation Economics](https://lowob.com/research/demand-generation-economics/)

Published 2026-11-17. Demand generation should be managed on the cost of a qualified opportunity and the time it takes a won customer to pay that cost back, not on lead volume. Forrester's research finds fewer than 1% of leads convert to closed deals, so a programme optimised for leads is optimised for the wrong thing. Work backwards from a payback target and every channel gets a ceiling: the most it can spend to produce one qualified opportunity. The harder part is that buyers are, by 6sense's estimate, nearly 70% through their process before they speak to a seller, so the spend that creates demand is the spend that is hardest to measure.

## [Discount Governance](https://lowob.com/research/discount-governance/)

Published 2026-11-17. Discount governance is the set of rules that decides who may offer what discount, in exchange for what, and how the decision is recorded. It matters because price changes have outsized effects on profit: the classic Harvard Business Review analysis found that a 1% improvement in realised price lifted operating profit by 11.1% for an average large firm, against 3.3% for a 1% rise in volume. Most firms govern discounts with an approval chain and nothing else, which slows deals without teaching anyone anything. A working system sets discount bands, attaches a trade to every concession, rules within a stated time and records the reason, so that the pattern of exceptions can be reviewed and the bands improved.

## [The Enterprise AI and Commercial System Glossary](https://lowob.com/research/enterprise-ai-glossary/)

Published 2026-11-17. This glossary defines the terms used across The Build Order and the wider enterprise AI market in plain English. Each entry gives a working definition, notes where vendors use the word differently, and links to the research or explainer that goes deeper. Terms are grouped by layer of the brain: agents and reasoning, the wiring, the record, governance and risk, pricing, and the commercial system.

## [Events That Pay Back](https://lowob.com/research/events-that-pay-back/)

Published 2026-11-17. An event pays back when the meetings it produces lead to pipeline that would not otherwise have existed, at a cost the firm would accept from any other channel. Most B2B event spend cannot show that, because the case for it is written after the event, from badge scans and impressions. In-person contact still matters: McKinsey's 2024 B2B Pulse survey of nearly 4,000 decision makers found 41% prefer in-person channels when dealing with new suppliers. The fix is a short business case written before booking, meetings set before arrival, a follow-up rule, and a comparison of target accounts met against those not met over two quarters.

## [Forecasting That Holds](https://lowob.com/research/forecasting-that-holds/)

Published 2026-11-17. A forecast holds when the firm can say, before the period ends, how far off its last ten forecasts were and why. Most cannot. Gartner found that only 45% of sales leaders and sellers had high confidence in their organisation's forecast accuracy, and a Forrester Consulting study found that 55% of revenue teams missed their quarterly forecast by more than 10% on average. The method is rarely the main problem. Stage probabilities are borrowed from software defaults, close dates slip without consequence and past calls are overwritten instead of scored. The fix is to record each forecast call with its basis, compare it with the outcome and use the error to correct the next call.

## [From Founder-Led to Team-Led Marketing](https://lowob.com/research/from-founder-led-to-team-led-marketing/)

Published 2026-11-17. Marketing moves from founder-led to team-led when decision rights transfer in a deliberate order and the founder's reasoning is handed over in writing, not when a marketing hire starts. The usual failures are a first hire asked to generate demand before the position is settled, and a founder who approves every post for two years. The evidence argues for structure: McKinsey found only 46% of respondents rated delegated decisions high quality, against 65% for big bets, and Gartner found 69% of buyers see inconsistencies between a supplier's website and its sellers. Transfer execution first, then channels and budget, then messaging. The founder keeps the position and a voice, not the approvals.

## [Gateway 3: When Commercial Is Ready to Share Its Brain](https://lowob.com/research/gateway-three-when-commercial-is-ready-to-share-its-brain/)

Published 2026-11-17. Gateway 3 is the point at which the commercial record is extended to delivery, finance and people. It should be passed on evidence, not ambition: one decision class recorded for at least two quarters, outcomes written back, value reported in money, permissions holding, an export tested, and a named owner in the next function asking for the record. Delivery comes first because it inherits the client from sales. Finance comes second because it already audits the dollar figures from Gateway 2. People decisions come last, because hiring, promotion and performance carry legal duties that commercial decisions do not, including EU AI Act high-risk obligations for employment systems from 2 December 2027. At each step the owner changes, the outcome lag lengthens and the ceiling on autonomy drops.

## [Gateway 2: Put a Dollar Figure on Every Commercial Decision](https://lowob.com/research/gateway-two-a-dollar-figure-on-every-commercial-decision/)

Published 2026-11-17. Gateway 2 asks one thing of the commercial record: that every recorded decision carries the money it puts at stake, and that the realised value is written back when the outcome arrives. Without that, a build can only report activity: drafts produced, hours saved, seats active. Finance does not fund activity twice. The evidence says most firms are stuck there. In PwC's 2026 Global CEO Survey, 56% of 4,454 CEOs reported no significant financial benefit from AI to date. The fix is not a better model. It is two fields on the record, a quarterly reconciliation and an honest line for the human time the system consumes.

## [Gateway 0: Three Decisions Before Any AI Tool](https://lowob.com/research/gateway-zero-three-decisions-before-any-ai-tool/)

Published 2026-11-17. Before buying any AI tool, answer three questions. Who owns the build, with protected time each week? Which suite is the company's system of record, Google Workspace or Microsoft 365? And which CRM will people actually keep current? Regulated firms add a fourth: who decides what data the system may see. Most stalled builds we encounter skipped at least one of these, and each is cheaper to answer up front than to unwind later.

## [How to Measure AI ROI in a Commercial Team](https://lowob.com/research/how-to-measure-ai-roi/)

Published 2026-11-17. AI return on investment in a commercial team is the money gained from decisions and work the AI informed, minus what it cost to run, including the time people spend reviewing its output. It cannot be read from seats activated or hours saved. It is measured by attaching a value at stake to each decision when it is made, writing back the realised value later against a comparison, and netting off tool cost and review time. That is Gateway 2 in **lowob**'s Build Order.

## [How to Raise for an Emerging Tech Company: The Complete Guide](https://lowob.com/research/how-to-raise-for-an-emerging-tech-company/)

Published 2026-11-17. Raising for an emerging tech company in 2026 means raising in a market with record totals and narrow access. US venture deal value reached $515.8 billion through September, but rounds of $100 million or more took 87.5% of first-half dollars, and seed capital on Carta's platform fell from $6.5 billion to $3.8 billion year on year. The companies that raise normal-sized rounds do four things: they raise against evidence, not narrative; they run the round like a sales process; they read pass reasons when it stalls; and they adjust for what their category changes, whether that is inference cost, a licence, a long sales cycle or a platform-dependent audience.

## [Human-in-the-Loop vs Human-on-the-Loop](https://lowob.com/research/human-in-the-loop-vs-human-on-the-loop/)

Published 2026-11-17. Human-in-the-loop means a person approves each AI output before it takes effect. Human-on-the-loop means the system acts on its own while a person monitors, reviews afterwards and can intervene or stop it. In the loop is safer and slower; on the loop is faster and depends on the monitoring being real. The choice should be made task by task, based on whether the action can be undone and who it reaches.

## [Intent Data vs First-Party Data](https://lowob.com/research/intent-data-vs-first-party-data/)

Published 2026-11-17. Intent data, in the sense most vendors sell it, is a third-party feed that infers which companies are researching a topic, based on content consumed across publisher networks. First-party data is information a firm collects directly from its own customers and prospects: CRM records, website and product behaviour, email engagement, support tickets and billing. Intent sees research before a buyer reaches you, at company level and with uncertainty. First-party data sees less of the market but is owned, more accurate and often tied to named people. For most B2B firms, first-party data is the cheaper and more reliable place to start.

## [Lead Scoring vs Account Scoring](https://lowob.com/research/lead-scoring-vs-account-scoring/)

Published 2026-11-17. Lead scoring ranks individual people by how well they fit your ideal customer and how engaged they are. Account scoring ranks companies, combining how well the company fits with the engagement of everyone you know there. Lead scores answer "who should we call?"; account scores answer "which companies should we work on?". Because B2B purchases are made by groups, most firms should let the account score set priority and the lead score pick the person.

## [LLM Observability vs Application Monitoring](https://lowob.com/research/llm-observability-vs-apm/)

Published 2026-11-17. Application performance monitoring (APM) tells you whether a service is available, fast and free of errors. LLM observability tells you what a model or agent was given, what it did, what it cost and whether the result was any good. A model call can return in under a second with a success code and still be wrong, so APM alone cannot see the failures that matter most in AI systems.

## [Long Context Windows vs RAG](https://lowob.com/research/long-context-vs-rag/)

Published 2026-11-17. Long context means putting whole documents directly into the model's prompt and letting it read everything. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) means searching a store first and giving the model only the passages that look relevant. Long context is simpler and often more accurate on a bounded set of documents. RAG is cheaper, scales to large and changing collections, and is the natural place to enforce who may see what.

## [LTV:CAC vs CAC Payback: Which Unit Economics Metric to Trust](https://lowob.com/research/ltv-cac-vs-cac-payback/)

Published 2026-11-17. LTV:CAC is the ratio of a customer's estimated lifetime value, usually lifetime gross profit, to the cost of acquiring that customer. CAC payback is the number of months of gross profit it takes to recover the acquisition cost. Both start from the same inputs. The difference is that LTV:CAC needs a forecast of how long customers stay, while payback does not. For most firms of 20 to 500 people, payback is the number to trust for budget decisions, and LTV:CAC is a check once several years of retention data exist.

## [Market Maps That Sales Actually Uses](https://lowob.com/research/market-maps-that-sales-actually-uses/)

Published 2026-11-17. A market map that sales uses is not a slide. It is a list of named accounts held in the CRM, each with a segment, a tier, the trigger that makes it timely, an owner and a status, refreshed on a fixed rhythm. Most maps fail because they describe the market rather than direct the work. Gartner found 84% of sales leaders said analytics had less influence on sales performance than expected, and Forrester found sellers choosing from an average of 1,400 sales assets. Another document will not help. A working map turns the segment choice from Part 3 into a weekly list of who to call and why.

## [Marketplace Listings for B2B Sellers](https://lowob.com/research/marketplace-listings-for-b2b/)

Published 2026-11-17. A cloud marketplace listing lets a buyer purchase your software or services through a platform such as AWS Marketplace, Microsoft's marketplace or Google Cloud's, with the charge landing on the bill they already pay the platform. For most B2B sellers its value is procurement, not discovery. A deal that would take months to pass vendor onboarding can close as a line item on an existing cloud bill, under terms the buyer's legal team may already accept, and some marketplace purchases count toward the buyer's committed spend with the platform. The work is in private offers, finance operations and sales compensation, not in the listing page.

## [MCP vs A2A: How the Two Agent Protocols Fit Together](https://lowob.com/research/mcp-vs-a2a/)

Published 2026-11-17. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standard for connecting an AI application to tools and data, such as a CRM search or a document store. The Agent2Agent protocol (A2A) is a standard for one agent to hand a task to another agent, often from a different vendor, and follow its progress. MCP is how an agent uses a tool; A2A is how an agent delegates work. Most multi-agent systems will use both, and neither keeps the record of who decided what.

## [MCP vs API Integrations: What Changes and What Does Not](https://lowob.com/research/mcp-vs-api-integrations/)

Published 2026-11-17. An API integration is code that a developer writes against one system's interface, following a path fixed in advance. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets an AI application connect to many systems the same way, discover what tools each one offers, and let the model decide when to call them. MCP changes who chooses the call and how connections are packaged. It does not replace the API underneath, and it does not remove the need for permissions, clean data or a person approving actions.

## [Measuring Brand in B2B](https://lowob.com/research/measuring-brand-in-b2b/)

Published 2026-11-17. Measuring brand in B2B means tracking whether buyers think of you, and rank you, before they contact anyone. That ranking now happens early: 6sense's 2025 survey of more than 4,000 buyers found 94% of buying groups had ranked preferred vendors before first contact, and the favourite usually won. Attribution systems see only what happens after that moment, which is why brand budgets are cut first and defended worst. Five measures hold up in B2B: share of search, shortlist rate, mental availability against buying situations, branded demand, and win rate and price when the buyer already knew you. Each needs adapting when a market has a few hundred buyers rather than millions.

## [NIST AI RMF vs ISO/IEC 42001](https://lowob.com/research/nist-ai-rmf-vs-iso-42001/)

Published 2026-11-17. The NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) is free, voluntary guidance from the US National Institute of Standards and Technology on identifying and managing AI risk. ISO/IEC 42001 is an international standard that sets requirements for an AI management system, which an accredited auditor can certify. In practice, firms use the NIST framework as a vocabulary and checklist, and ISO/IEC 42001 when a customer or regulator wants proof.

## [Gateway 1: Nothing Sends Without a Person](https://lowob.com/research/nothing-sends-without-a-person/)

Published 2026-11-17. Gateway 1 is a single rule: nothing an agent produces leaves the company until a named person approves it, and every approval is logged with who, when and what they saw. It is the most common control in serious agent deployments because it addresses the leading security risks for AI systems, gives regulated firms the evidence supervisors ask for, and keeps the first mistakes internal. It only works if reviewers actually check, so the gate needs its own measures.

## [NRR vs GRR: Which Retention Number to Report](https://lowob.com/research/nrr-vs-grr/)

Published 2026-11-17. Net revenue retention (NRR) is what a group of existing customers pays you now, divided by what the same customers paid a year ago, including expansion. Gross revenue retention (GRR) uses the same cohort but excludes expansion, so it shows only what you kept after churn and downgrades, and it cannot exceed 100%. NRR tells you whether the base grows on its own; GRR tells you how much of it leaks. Report both, because the same NRR can hide very different levels of churn.

## [Partner Channel Design](https://lowob.com/research/partner-channel-design/)

Published 2026-11-17. Partner channel design is the set of decisions a firm makes before recruiting partners: what job partners do in the sale, which partner types fit that job, how each is paid, what earns a higher tier, and who owns the customer when two parties touch the same deal. The stakes are large in technology markets: Canalys estimated that 70% of worldwide IT spending in 2025 flowed through partners. Most mid-size programmes skip the design and start with a partner agreement and a logo page. The result is a long list of signed partners and a short list of partner-sourced revenue.

## [Positioning for Complex Markets](https://lowob.com/research/positioning-for-complex-markets/)

Published 2026-11-17. Positioning is the choice of which buyer you serve, which problem you solve and which alternative you replace. In complex markets that choice has to work without a seller in the room, across a buying group of a dozen people, against a competitor that is usually inaction. Forrester's 2024 study found 13 people involved in the average purchase and 91% of purchases stalling at some point. Research by Matt Dixon and Ted McKenna found 40% to 60% of lost deals end in no decision. A position built for those conditions names the status quo as the alternative, gives each role in the buying group a reason to agree, and carries proof a buyer can check alone.

## [Pricing Architecture for Services Firms](https://lowob.com/research/pricing-architecture-for-services-firms/)

Published 2026-11-17. A pricing architecture is the set of rules that turns a firm's rate card into the fee it actually keeps: the fee model, the packages, the discount and exception rules, the scope change terms and the payment terms. Most services firms have a rate card and no architecture, so the realised price is set deal by deal. That matters because price is the strongest profit lever available. Marn and Rosiello's classic *Harvard Business Review* analysis found a 1% price improvement, with volume unchanged, lifted operating profit by 11.1%, against 3.3% for a 1% volume gain. Design the architecture once, measure the gap between list and pocket price, and record every exception so the rules can learn.

## [Pricing Experiments in B2B](https://lowob.com/research/pricing-experiments-in-b2b/)

Published 2026-11-17. A pricing experiment is a deliberate, recorded change to price, packaging or discount rules, made for a defined group of customers or deals, with a measure and a date to judge it. B2B firms seldom have the volume or the anonymity to run consumer-style A/B tests on list price, but they can test price for new cohorts, test packaging, test discount guardrails and run structured buyer research. The payoff is large: Marn and Rosiello's 1992 analysis of 2,463 companies found a 1% price improvement lifted operating profit by 11.1%. The discipline is the same as any test: decide in advance what result would change the decision.

## [Prompt Engineering vs Context Engineering](https://lowob.com/research/prompt-engineering-vs-context-engineering/)

Published 2026-11-17. Prompt engineering is the practice of writing and structuring a model's instructions so its output meets a requirement. Context engineering is the wider practice of choosing everything the model sees at each step: instructions, retrieved documents and records, tool results and conversation history. Prompting mostly fixes format, tone and task framing. Context mostly fixes accuracy. A well-written prompt cannot rescue a model that was handed the wrong facts.

## [Proposal Standards That Win and Teach](https://lowob.com/research/proposal-standards/)

Published 2026-11-17. A proposal standard is a short, written rule set that says what every proposal must prove, which sections it must contain, who reviews it and what gets recorded once the buyer decides. It matters because the proposal is now read mostly by people the seller never meets. Forrester's 2024 survey found an average of 13 people involved in a B2B purchase, and Gartner's 2026 survey found two-thirds of buyers preferred a rep-free experience. A proposal that wins makes the case for change, the case for this supplier and the case for acting now, in that order, for readers who were not in the room. A proposal that teaches is tagged with its outcome and the buyer's reasons, so the next one starts from evidence.

## [Qualification Frameworks Compared](https://lowob.com/research/qualification-frameworks-compared/)

Published 2026-11-17. A sales qualification framework is a fixed set of questions a seller must answer, with evidence from the buyer, before a deal is treated as real. The common ones test different things. BANT checks whether the buyer can buy now. CHAMP starts from the buyer's problem. MEDDICC maps how the buying organisation will decide. SPICED tests whether the problem is urgent enough to act on. Benchmark data suggests that teams which apply any framework consistently outperform those which do not, and that the framework matters less than whether its answers decide stage movement. Pick the one that matches the deal you sell, then make every letter a field.

## [RAG vs Fine-Tuning: Which One Your Use Case Needs](https://lowob.com/research/rag-vs-fine-tuning/)

Published 2026-11-17. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) gives a model relevant passages from your own documents at the moment it answers. Fine-tuning further trains the model on your examples so that it behaves differently every time. RAG is the tool for knowledge: facts, prices, policies and anything that changes. Fine-tuning is the tool for behaviour: format, tone and consistency on a narrow, repeated task. Most commercial use cases need RAG first, and many never need fine-tuning at all.

## [Referral Partners Without Leakage](https://lowob.com/research/referral-partners-without-leakage/)

Published 2026-11-17. A referral partner is a firm or person who introduces a buyer and steps back: an adviser, a consultant, an accountant, a complementary vendor or a customer. Referral programmes in B2B rarely fail for lack of introductions. They fail because value leaks between the introduction and the payment, in both directions. The vendor pays for deals it already had, the partner sees its introductions go cold or its fees arrive late, and both carry regulatory risk if contact data or payments are handled loosely. Six leaks account for most of the loss, and each is closed by a rule written before the first referral, not after the first dispute.

## [Renewals and Expansion](https://lowob.com/research/renewals-and-expansion/)

Published 2026-11-17. Renewals and expansion are how a firm grows revenue from customers it already has. For most mid-size B2B firms the existing base is barely growing on its own: a KeyBanc and Sapphire Ventures survey of more than 100 private SaaS companies put median net revenue retention at about 101% and gross retention at about 90%. The firms that do better treat renewal as a process with a calendar, not a contract date. They decide each renewal months ahead, choose the expansion motion that fits the account's signals and record the reason for every renewal decision, so the next cohort can be predicted rather than hoped for.

## [RevOps vs Sales Ops: What Changed and Why It Matters](https://lowob.com/research/revops-vs-sales-ops/)

Published 2026-11-17. Sales operations (sales ops) is the function that gives a sales team its processes, tools, data and plans: territories, quotas, compensation, CRM administration and the forecast. Revenue operations (RevOps) runs the same kind of work across the whole revenue line, so marketing, sales and customer success share one set of definitions, one data model and one set of systems. The change is one of scope and ownership. It matters more now because AI tools read across all three functions and inherit every disagreement between them.

## [Sales Capacity and Quota Setting](https://lowob.com/research/sales-capacity-and-quota-setting/)

Published 2026-11-17. Sales capacity is the revenue a team can realistically produce in a period, given who is in seat, how long new hires take to ramp and what share of quota sellers usually attain. Quota setting should start from that number and then reconcile it with the target, not the other way round. The Bridge Group's 2026 study of 158 B2B companies found 48% of account executives at quota, down from 51% in 2024, with average ramp time at 6.2 months, the longest in the study's history. A plan that ignores those two figures is a wish with a spreadsheet attached.

## [Segment Selection With Evidence](https://lowob.com/research/segment-selection-with-evidence/)

Published 2026-11-17. Segment selection is the decision about which groups of buyers the firm pursues first, which it serves when they arrive, and which it declines. Most firms make it on market size and logo appeal. The better evidence is usually in the CRM already: win rate, deal size, cycle length and retention by segment, combined into a value per opportunity. Gartner's research on key accounts found that customers elevated mainly for their large spend were 51% less likely to increase it over time, a reminder that size is not the same as potential. Choose on evidence, check the chosen segment is large enough from the bottom up, and record the choice with its disqualifiers and a review date.

## [Semantic Layer vs Knowledge Graph](https://lowob.com/research/semantic-layer-vs-knowledge-graph/)

Published 2026-11-17. A semantic layer fixes how business terms and numbers are calculated, such as revenue, active client or win rate, so every report and agent gets the same answer. A knowledge graph records how things connect, such as which person signed which contract and which proposal replaced which, so a system can follow those links. The semantic layer answers "how much"; the graph answers "how is this related". Both make business meaning explicit, and most commercial teams need the definitions first.

## [SOC 2 for AI Vendors: What It Covers and What It Does Not](https://lowob.com/research/soc-2-for-ai-vendors/)

Published 2026-11-17. SOC 2 is an independent auditor's report on whether a service organisation's controls meet the AICPA Trust Services Criteria for security and, optionally, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy. For an AI vendor it tells you a good deal about access control, change management and incident handling, and very little about whether the model is accurate, unbiased or well monitored. The current criteria date from 2017; the AICPA proposed a revision with AI-specific points of focus in October 2026.

## [SOC 2 vs ISO 27001 for AI Vendors](https://lowob.com/research/soc-2-vs-iso-27001/)

Published 2026-11-17. SOC 2 is an attestation: a CPA firm examines a service organisation's description of its system and tests its controls against the AICPA Trust Services Criteria, then issues a restricted report. ISO/IEC 27001 is a certification: an accredited certification body confirms that the organisation runs an information security management system (ISMS) that meets the standard's requirements. SOC 2 shows how specific controls performed; ISO/IEC 27001 shows that a management system exists and keeps improving. Neither currently tests whether an AI model is accurate or well governed.

## [The Build Order for B2B SaaS](https://lowob.com/research/the-build-order-for-b2b-saas/)

Published 2026-11-17. The Build Order holds in B2B SaaS, with one change: product usage data joins the context layer early, because in a recurring-revenue business the strongest commercial signal is what customers do inside the product. The first decisions worth recording are renewals, expansion offers and the discounts attached to both, since retention drives growth more than new logos for most private SaaS firms. The sector's wall is the content customers store inside the product. Usage metadata can inform a renewal brief. A customer's own records, tickets and documents cannot, because the vendor holds them as a processor on the customer's instructions.

## [The Build Order for Crypto and Digital Assets](https://lowob.com/research/the-build-order-for-crypto-and-digital-assets/)

Published 2026-11-17. Crypto and digital-asset companies can run The Build Order as written. The commercial line is distribution: which integrations to pursue, which grants to fund, which creators to pay and how much to spend on incentives. Two things are different. First, Gateway 1 is stricter than in any other sector, because a post on X, Telegram or Discord can be a marketing communication under the EU's MiCA regulation or a financial promotion under UK law, and MiCA's transitional period for unauthorised providers ended on 1 July 2026. Second, the wall is physical as well as informational: signing keys, treasury wallets and deployment credentials must never be reachable by any agent. Chainalysis counted more than $3.4bn stolen from crypto services and users in 2025, with attacks on private key infrastructure and signing processes behind the largest losses.

## [The Build Order for Financial Services and Fintech](https://lowob.com/research/the-build-order-for-financial-services-and-fintech/)

Published 2026-11-17. Financial services is one of two sectors where The Build Order bends. The commercial line is still the right place to start, but the decision record and the audit trail come before the first agent rather than after it. The reason is supervisory. FINRA's 2026 oversight report covers AI agents for the first time and asks firms how they will track agent actions and decisions. The US banking agencies' April 2026 model risk guidance, SR 26-2, explicitly excludes generative and agentic AI from its scope, which leaves firms to govern those tools through their own risk frameworks. The EU AI Act's high-risk obligations, including credit scoring, now apply from 2 December 2027 after the Digital Omnibus. In each case the question a supervisor asks is the same: show us what happened, who approved it and why. A firm that builds the record first can answer it.

## [The Build Order for Healthcare and Life Sciences](https://lowob.com/research/the-build-order-for-healthcare-and-life-sciences/)

Published 2026-11-17. Healthcare and life sciences is one of the two sectors where The Build Order bends. Here compliance comes first: privacy and promotional review precede any commercial agent. HIPAA requires written authorisation before protected health information is used for most marketing. Washington's My Health My Data Act requires affirmative consent before consumer health data is even collected. FDA's promotion office sent nearly 100 enforcement letters in a single week in September 2025, against five in each of 2023 and 2024. So the walls, the review gate and the record are built before the first agent, and the first agent works for the review committee rather than the field team. Patient data never reaches the commercial build.

## [The Build Order for Industrial Distribution](https://lowob.com/research/the-build-order-for-industrial-distribution/)

Published 2026-11-17. In industrial distribution the commercial line is quoting. Inside sales teams decide all day which requests to quote, what discount to give against the price book and what lead time to promise, and each quote is won or lost within days. That makes distribution the fastest-learning sector in this series. The store is the ERP rather than a CRM, and the context layer is mostly the price book and the specification library. The walls are specific: competitors' non-public prices must never feed the quoting logic, supplier cost and rebate terms must never surface in a customer-facing draft, and export-controlled technical data must stay behind its own access controls.

## [The Build Order for Media and Publishing](https://lowob.com/research/the-build-order-for-media-and-publishing/)

Published 2026-11-17. Publishers can run The Build Order as written, provided the context layer is split in two. The commercial line is advertising, sponsorship, subscriptions, events and, increasingly, licensing content to AI companies. The wall is the newsroom: sales context must never reach editorial, and confidential reporting must never reach sales or an outside model. The pressure to build is real. Publishers surveyed by the Reuters Institute in early 2026 expect search referrals to fall by more than 40% over three years, and Chartbeat data in the same report showed organic search traffic to over 2,500 sites down 33% in a year. Pew Research found Google users clicked a traditional result on 8% of visits when an AI summary appeared, against 15% without one. Meanwhile the EU AI Act's transparency rules, in force since 2 August 2026, make attributable editorial responsibility the condition for publishing AI-assisted text without a label.

## [The Build Order for Professional Services Firms](https://lowob.com/research/the-build-order-for-professional-services-firms/)

Published 2026-11-17. Law, accounting and consulting firms can run The Build Order almost as written. The commercial line is real and well defined: which work to pitch for, what fee to quote, and which write-offs to accept. What changes is the wiring. The same partners who win the work also deliver it, so their inboxes hold both pitch context and client confidences, and the conflict walls a regulator already expects must be built into the context layer on day one. The evidence says firms are using AI faster than they can measure it. Thomson Reuters' 2026 survey of more than 1,500 professionals found 40% say their organisation uses generative AI, while only 18% say it tracks return on investment. Billable utilisation fell to 66.4% in 2025 in SPI Research's benchmark, which makes the protected time Gateway 0 requires unusually expensive to give.

## [The Build Order for Retail, DTC and Luxury](https://lowob.com/research/the-build-order-for-retail-dtc-and-luxury/)

Published 2026-11-17. The Build Order holds in retail, DTC and luxury, but client consent governs what can be connected. The commercial line runs through clienteling: advisers, their client books and the decisions about who to invite, what to offer and when. The law sets the outer limit on that context. GDPR gives people an absolute right to object to direct marketing, including profiling; California's updated CCPA regulations took effect on 1 January 2026; and twenty US states have comprehensive privacy laws in effect this year. What clients told an adviser in confidence sets a tighter limit still. The first agent prompts the adviser. It never writes to the client.

## [The Ten Commercial Decisions Worth Recording](https://lowob.com/research/the-commercial-decisions-worth-recording/)

Published 2026-11-17. The record is the part of the brain a company must own, and it pays back fastest where decisions are frequent, similar, quickly graded and later defended. On the commercial line, ten decision classes meet that test, from discount exceptions and lead qualification to campaign spend and closed-lost reasons. Each record needs five fields (reason, owner, status, expected outcome and a date to check) and the outcome written back when it arrives. Start with one class, not ten.

## [The Commercial Operating Rhythm: Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly](https://lowob.com/research/the-commercial-operating-rhythm/)

Published 2026-11-17. A commercial operating rhythm is the fixed sequence of meetings in which a firm reviews its commercial numbers and makes its recurring commercial decisions. It has three cadences. Weekly, the team decides on deals and account coverage. Monthly, it sets the forecast and moves channel and campaign effort. Quarterly, it grades the strategic choices on segment, position, price and the market map against outcomes. The rhythm matters because commercial decisions are frequent and decision time is poorly used: McKinsey's 2019 survey found managers spend 37% of their time making decisions and that most of that time is used ineffectively. A good rhythm uses one set of numbers, ends each meeting with recorded decisions, and is the point where the commercial system writes its outcomes back.

## [The Commercial System: What It Is, and Why Most Firms Run Without One](https://lowob.com/research/the-commercial-system-what-it-is/)

Published 2026-11-17. A commercial system is the connected set of choices, definitions, records and routines by which a firm decides whom to serve, creates demand, reaches buyers and wins and keeps revenue. We split it into four parts: Strategy, Growth, Distribution and Revenue. Most firms run all four as activity rather than as a system, with separate definitions and tools, and the money is lost at the seams. The commercial system is also what The Build Order's brain runs on: the brain starts at the commercial line because decisions there are frequent and quickly graded, but it can only learn from a system that has agreed what its words mean.

## [The Context Layer, Followed Through One Account](https://lowob.com/research/the-context-layer-followed-through-one-account/)

Published 2026-11-17. A context layer is the wiring that lets AI read a company's own systems: connectors into email, CRM, documents and calls; retrieval that respects existing permissions; and shared definitions so that every agent means the same thing by "active client". It should be rented, not built. The decisions that matter are what to connect first, what to wall off, and how to mark which information is current. Even done well, it cannot retrieve a decision nobody recorded, which is why the record comes next.

## [The EU AI Act for Commercial Teams: What Applies and When](https://lowob.com/research/the-eu-ai-act-for-commercial-teams/)

Published 2026-11-17. For a sales, marketing or customer team, the EU AI Act mostly applies through four routes: a short list of banned practices, a duty to support AI literacy, transparency rules for chatbots, deepfakes and AI-written public-interest text, and stricter rules if a tool falls into a high-risk category such as recruitment or credit scoring. Most commercial teams are deployers of other firms' tools, not providers. After the Digital Omnibus, Annex III high-risk obligations apply from 2 December 2027.

## [The First AI Agent Should Be Boring](https://lowob.com/research/the-first-ai-agent-should-be-boring/)

Published 2026-11-17. The first agent on the commercial line should be boring: a job that happens often, can be checked quickly, does little damage if it goes wrong, and that people dislike doing. Autonomous outbound, the most requested first agent, fails all four tests. A pipeline clerk passes them: it keeps the CRM current, flags stale deals and drafts follow-ups into a queue, and it never sends anything itself. Measure it for four weeks before giving it anything else.

## [The Handover From Sales to Delivery](https://lowob.com/research/the-handover-from-sales-to-delivery/)

Published 2026-11-17. The handover from sales to delivery is the point where a won deal becomes work, and where most of what the deal team learned is lost. A good handover passes on more than the contract: the promises made, the buying group and its politics, the concessions and why they were granted, the risks raised, and what success means to the buyer. Forrester's 2024 research found 81% of B2B buyers dissatisfied with the provider they chose. The handover cannot fix a bad sale, but it is the cheapest place to stop a good sale turning into a disappointed customer.

## [The Permission Problem: When Commercial Context Leaks](https://lowob.com/research/the-permission-problem-when-commercial-context-leaks/)

Published 2026-11-17. The assistants and context layers sold to mid-size firms are permission-aware: they only retrieve what the user could already open. That is the right design, and it is also the problem, because most firms' permissions were never meant to be searched. A pricing sheet shared "with anyone in the company" three years ago was safe while nobody could find it. Once an assistant can, it is not. Commercial context leaks by three paths: oversharing through inherited permissions, cross-client leakage when an agent mixes one account's context with another's, and prompt injection through content an outsider controls. Each has a control a firm without a security team can run. Most of them belong in the context step of the build, before any agent drafts for a client.

## [The RFP Nobody Can Answer Yet](https://lowob.com/research/the-rfp-nobody-can-answer-yet/)

Published 2026-11-17. More of the requests for proposals reaching us ask for three things in one brief: AI tooling, a context layer and an "enterprise brain". Very few say who will own the work, what success looks like or what should happen first. Vendors answer these briefs in incompatible ways because nobody has shipped the full brain; what exists, at scale, is the context layer. The Build Order is our answer to the missing sequence: decide three things before buying any tool, build on the commercial line first, and pass a named gateway before each next layer.

## [The Same Build in Four Industries](https://lowob.com/research/the-same-build-in-four-industries/)

Published 2026-11-17. We ran The Build Order through four composite firms in different sectors: a mid-market lender, a regional publisher, an industrial parts distributor and a luxury jeweller. The commercial line was the right place to start in all four, the wiring was necessary but not sufficient, and the best first agent was always unglamorous. The wider evidence points the same way. Validity's 2026 survey of 500 marketers found only 21% considered their CRM data very well prepared for AI, a reminder that every one of these firms started with a store that needed work before any agent could rely on it. Salesforce's 2026 State of Sales survey of more than 4,000 sales professionals found sellers spend about 40% of their time selling, which is why the first agents in all four firms targeted preparation and administration rather than the conversation itself. And Gartner's forecast that over 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by 2027, on cost, unclear value or weak risk controls, describes exactly what a boring first agent and a logged gate are designed to avoid.

## [Thought Leadership That Sales Can Use](https://lowob.com/research/thought-leadership-that-sales-can-use/)

Published 2026-11-17. Thought leadership pays when a seller can use it in a conversation to help a buyer decide, and most of it is never used that way. The evidence on buying points to why that use matters: Gartner's 2026 survey found confident buyers were twice as likely to report a high-quality deal, and Challenger's analysis of 2.5 million sales calls found around half of lost deals ended in no decision. A published position becomes usable when it is converted into five things a seller can carry: a discovery question, a diagnostic, a business case line, an objection answer and a first step. The loop closes when what sellers hear flows back into the positions.

## [Vector Database vs Knowledge Graph](https://lowob.com/research/vector-database-vs-knowledge-graph/)

Published 2026-11-17. A vector database stores text as embeddings, lists of numbers that capture meaning, and finds the items closest to a question. A knowledge graph stores facts as entities and the named relationships between them, such as "account A is owned by person B". Vectors are good at "find me things like this". Graphs are good at "show me how these things connect, and prove it". Many AI systems use both, and the products are converging.

## [What AI Agents Can Do: A Task Directory for Commercial Teams](https://lowob.com/research/what-ai-agents-can-do-task-directory/)

Published 2026-11-17. This directory rates sixty commercial tasks by how far an AI agent can take them today. Each row gives the highest sensible autonomy level on **lowob**'s five-step scale, a plain reliability rating, the main risk, and the control that has to be in place. Use it to choose first agents, to challenge vendor claims, and to decide where a person must stay in the loop. Ratings reflect our working view for mid-size commercial teams in late 2026 and will move as capability improves.

## [What AI Agents Still Cannot Do, and How to Tell Before You Buy](https://lowob.com/research/what-ai-agents-still-cannot-do/)

Published 2026-11-17. AI agents can now complete multi-hour software tasks half the time, and they still cannot be trusted alone with most commercial work. Across the sixty tasks in the **lowob** directory, none is rated for level 4 (act alone), and six are rated low reliability: pricing, discounts, autonomous outbound, budget moves, shared definitions and access changes. Five failure patterns explain why: long horizons, changed facts, prompt injection, excessive agency, and judgement calls with no graded precedent. Gartner expects over 40% of agentic AI projects to be cancelled by the end of 2027. A buyer who asks seven plain questions before signing can avoid being one of them.

## [What Are AI Evals?](https://lowob.com/research/what-are-ai-evals/)

Published 2026-11-17. AI evals, short for evaluations, are structured tests that measure whether an AI system does a specific task well. Each eval pairs a set of realistic inputs with a way of scoring the outputs, by exact match, by a person or by another model. Evals turn "it seems to work" into a number you can track across prompt changes, model upgrades and vendors. They are the basis for deciding how much autonomy an AI tool gets.

## [What Are AI Guardrails?](https://lowob.com/research/what-are-ai-guardrails/)

Published 2026-11-17. AI guardrails are controls placed around a language model that check its inputs, its outputs and the actions it takes against a set of rules. They can block harmful content, keep an assistant on topic, mask personal data, flag answers not supported by sources and limit which tools an agent may call. Guardrails reduce risk but do not remove it. The strongest ones are design choices: narrow permissions and a person approving anything that leaves the company.

## [What Are Embeddings?](https://lowob.com/research/what-are-embeddings/)

Published 2026-11-17. An embedding is a list of numbers that represents a piece of text, an image or another item, arranged so that items with similar meaning sit close together. Comparing those numbers lets software find related content without matching exact words. Embeddings power semantic search, recommendations and retrieval for AI assistants. They measure similarity, not truth, and the right model depends on the task.

## [What Are Pipeline Stage Definitions?](https://lowob.com/research/what-are-pipeline-stage-definitions/)

Published 2026-11-17. Pipeline stage definitions are the written rules for what must be true before an opportunity enters each stage of the sales pipeline. Good definitions are based on verifiable buyer actions, not seller feelings, and each stage has exit criteria that can be checked in the CRM. They are what make a stage-weighted forecast mean something, and what let an AI system read "stage" as a fact.

## [What Is a Buying Committee?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-buying-committee/)

Published 2026-11-17. A buying committee is the group of people at a customer organisation who take part in deciding a business-to-business purchase: those who use, evaluate, fund, approve and contract for it. Researchers call it the buying center; Gartner and Forrester call it the buying group. Recent surveys put it at five to 16 people, and conflict within it is common.

## [What Is a Closed-Lost Reason, and Why Does It Matter for AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-closed-lost-reason/)

Published 2026-11-17. A closed-lost reason is the value recorded in the CRM to explain why an opportunity was lost, usually chosen from a fixed list with a short note. It is the field that connects an outcome to a cause. For AI systems that score, forecast or recommend, it is the difference between knowing that deals are lost and knowing why, and without it they can only learn correlation.

## [What Is a Commercial Operating System?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-commercial-operating-system/)

Published 2026-11-17. A commercial operating system is the combined set of definitions, data, decision records, routines and tools a firm uses to find, win and keep clients. It is not a product. It is the agreed way the commercial line runs, written down and wired into the systems people use. Its test is whether a new hire, a board member or an AI agent would reach the same answer from the same records.

## [What Is a Computer-Use Agent?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-computer-use-agent/)

Published 2026-11-17. A computer-use agent is an AI agent that operates software the way a person does: it looks at screenshots and decides where to click, what to type and when to scroll. It can work in applications that have no API or connector. It is also slower, less reliable and more exposed to manipulation than an agent working through APIs. Providers advise running it on an isolated machine with minimal access, and asking a person to confirm anything with real-world consequences.

## [What Is a Context Window?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-context-window/)

Published 2026-11-17. A context window is all the text a language model can consider in a single request, including the response it is writing. It works as the model's working memory, separate from what it learned in training, and it is measured in tokens. Current frontier models offer windows of up to a million tokens. Research shows that accuracy falls as inputs grow, so choosing what goes in matters more than how much fits.

## [What Is a Customer Data Platform?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-customer-data-platform/)

Published 2026-11-17. A customer data platform (CDP) is packaged software that collects customer data from many sources, links it into one persistent profile per customer and shares those profiles with other systems, mostly for marketing. It differs from a CRM, which people work in, and a data warehouse, which holds history for analysis. Many B2B firms of 20 to 500 people can meet the need with a warehouse; a CDP earns its place when high-volume behavioural data must reach many channels quickly.

## [What Is a Data Processing Agreement for AI Tools?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-data-processing-agreement-for-ai/)

Published 2026-11-17. A data processing agreement (DPA) is the contract that governs how a vendor processes personal data on your behalf. Article 28 of the GDPR, and of the UK GDPR, requires one whenever a processor handles personal data for a controller, with a fixed set of terms. For an AI tool, the DPA shows whether the vendor may use your prompts beyond your instructions, which model providers receive them, and what is deleted at the end.

## [What Is a Deal Desk?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-deal-desk/)

Published 2026-11-17. A deal desk is a cross-functional team, or in a smaller firm a named role, that reviews deals falling outside standard pricing, discount or contract terms. It decides what can be approved, by whom and how fast. A good deal desk protects margin without becoming a queue: most deals pass straight through, and exceptions get a fast, recorded decision.

## [What Is a Decision Record?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-decision-record/)

Published 2026-11-17. A decision record is a short, dated entry that captures one decision: what was decided, why, who owns it, its current status and what outcome is expected. The format comes from software architecture, where Michael Nygard proposed architecture decision records in 2011. For a commercial team it is the part of the enterprise brain that no connector can supply, because a reason nobody wrote down cannot be retrieved.

## [What Is a Forecast Category?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-forecast-category/)

Published 2026-11-17. A forecast category is a label a seller puts on a deal to say how likely it is to close in the current period, typically Pipeline, Best Case or Commit. It is separate from the deal's stage, which says where the deal is in the sales process. The category is useful only when each label has a written definition and can differ from what the stage implies.

## [What Is a Go-to-Market Strategy?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-go-to-market-strategy/)

Published 2026-11-17. A go-to-market (GTM) strategy is the plan for how a company finds customers, persuades them to buy and does so at a cost that leaves a profitable business. **lowob** treats it as four decisions that must agree with each other: who exactly the buyer is, what they must believe, how trust moves from first contact to contract, and what evidence will show it is working. A list of channels and campaigns is not a GTM strategy; it is a list of tactics.

## [What Is a Golden Record?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-golden-record/)

Published 2026-11-17. A golden record is the single, trusted version of one real-world entity, such as a customer, account or product, assembled from matching records held in several systems. Entity resolution decides which records belong together; survivorship rules decide which value wins for each field. A good golden record keeps its source records, so every value can be traced.

## [What Is a Knowledge Graph (for AI)?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-knowledge-graph/)

Published 2026-11-17. A knowledge graph stores information as entities, such as companies, people, products and contracts, connected by named relationships, such as "works at", "signed" or "replaced". For AI, it gives a model a map of how facts connect, so it can answer questions that need several hops across sources. Text search finds similar passages; a graph follows links. Graphs help most where relationships matter and least where nobody maintains them.

## [What Is a Large Language Model (LLM)?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-large-language-model/)

Published 2026-11-17. A large language model (LLM) is a neural network trained on very large amounts of text to predict the next token, which lets it write, summarise, classify and answer questions in plain language. Most current LLMs use the Transformer architecture, first published in 2017. An LLM is the reasoning engine inside assistants and agents, not the whole product. It knows what it was trained on and what you put in front of it, nothing more.

## [What Is a Model Card?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-model-card/)

Published 2026-11-17. A model card is a short document that accompanies an AI model and reports what it is intended for, how it was evaluated, how it performs across different groups and conditions, what data it was trained on, and its known limits. The idea was proposed by Margaret Mitchell and colleagues in 2019 and is now the default format on model hubs. For a business buyer it is the first thing to read about a model, and the last word on nothing: it describes the model, not your use of it.

## [What Is a Multi-Agent System?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-multi-agent-system/)

Published 2026-11-17. A multi-agent system is a setup in which several AI agents, each with its own instructions, tools and context, work on parts of a task and pass results between them, usually under a lead agent that plans the work and combines the answers. It helps when work splits into independent parts that can run in parallel, such as broad research. It uses far more tokens than a single agent and fails in new ways when agents need to share context. Most commercial teams should start with one agent.

## [What Is a Mutual Action Plan?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-mutual-action-plan/)

Published 2026-11-17. A mutual action plan (MAP) is a shared document, agreed by buyer and seller, that lists the steps to a purchase decision and the start of work, each with a date and a named owner. It turns a close date the seller hopes for into a sequence the buyer has accepted. A plan the buyer never confirmed is a forecast assumption, not a mutual plan.

## [What Is a Partner Program?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-partner-program/)

Published 2026-11-17. A partner program is the written set of rules a company uses to work with other firms that refer, resell, deliver or integrate with its product. It defines who qualifies, what partners must do, what they receive, and how deals and customers are shared. A good program makes partner economics predictable for both sides; a weak one is a logo page and an unanswered inbox.

## [What Is a Quarterly Business Review (QBR)?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-quarterly-business-review/)

Published 2026-11-17. A quarterly business review (QBR) is a meeting held every three months in which a supplier and a customer review results against the goals they agreed, discuss what has changed in the customer's business and set goals for the next quarter. Its purpose is to keep both sides agreed on the value being delivered, well before a renewal date. A QBR that only presents usage statistics is a report, not a review. The test is whether the customer leaves with decisions and owners.

## [What Is a Reasoning Model?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-reasoning-model/)

Published 2026-11-17. A reasoning model is a large language model trained to work through a problem in a series of intermediate steps before giving its answer, spending extra computation at the moment of the request. OpenAI's o1, released in September 2024, and DeepSeek-R1, in January 2025, made the approach mainstream, and other major providers, including Anthropic, now offer a reasoning or "thinking" setting. Reasoning models are stronger on multi-step problems, slower and more expensive, and their visible reasoning is not a reliable account of why they answered as they did.

## [What Is a Sales Compensation Plan?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-sales-compensation-plan/)

Published 2026-11-17. A sales compensation plan is the written set of rules that decides how a seller's results turn into pay. It fixes target earnings, the split between base salary and incentive, the upside available for over-performance, which results count, the quota, and how payout rises or falls with attainment. Sellers read the plan more closely than any strategy document, so the plan is where strategy either reaches the field or does not.

## [What Is a Sales Engagement Platform?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-sales-engagement-platform/)

Published 2026-11-17. A sales engagement platform is software that runs a seller's outreach as sequences: planned series of emails, calls, social touches and tasks, sent or prompted on a schedule from one console. It logs every activity back to the CRM. It differs from marketing automation, which sends to lists, and from an AI SDR, which also decides what to write and send.

## [What Is a Sales Playbook?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-sales-playbook/)

Published 2026-11-17. A sales playbook is a written guide to how a team sells in defined situations: which buyers to pursue, what to ask, what to say, what evidence to share and what to do next at each stage. Its purpose is to make good practice repeatable across sellers. Most playbooks fail because they are long documents kept outside the CRM; the ones that work are short, situation-specific and built into the tools sellers already use.

## [What Is a Semantic Layer (Shared Definitions for AI)?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-semantic-layer/)

Published 2026-11-17. A semantic layer is a shared set of business definitions, such as revenue, active client or qualified lead, that every report, person and AI agent reads the same way. In data teams it is software that maps business terms to the tables and calculations underneath. For a commercial team it starts more simply: a handful of written definitions, each with an owner. Without one, two agents asked the same question can give two confident and different answers.

## [What Is a Small Language Model?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-small-language-model/)

Published 2026-11-17. A small language model (SLM) is a language model compact enough to run on ordinary hardware, such as a laptop, a phone or a single server, rather than a large cloud cluster. There is no fixed cut-off; NVIDIA researchers treat most models below about 10 billion parameters as small as of 2025. SLMs are cheaper and faster per request and can run where data must stay. They hold less general knowledge and handle open-ended reasoning less well, so they suit narrow, repeated tasks.

## [What Is a System of Record?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-system-of-record/)

Published 2026-11-17. A system of record is the one system a business treats as authoritative for a given type of data, such as the CRM for accounts and opportunities or the finance system for invoices. When two systems disagree, the system of record wins. It stores what is true now. It rarely stores why a decision was made, and that is the gap AI agents expose.

## [What Is a System Prompt?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-system-prompt/)

Published 2026-11-17. A system prompt is the standing set of instructions that a developer or operator gives an AI model before any user message. It defines the model's role, the task, the rules it should follow and the format of its answers. Model providers give it more authority than what users type. It is the right place to describe a job, and the wrong place to enforce security: OWASP advises that it should not be treated as secret or used as a control.

## [What Is a Token in AI, and Why Does It Drive Cost?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-token-in-ai/)

Published 2026-11-17. A token is the unit of text a language model reads and writes, usually a word or part of a word. In English, one token is roughly four characters, or about three-quarters of a word. Providers charge per million tokens, with separate prices for input and output, so token count is what turns an AI task into a bill. Agents use far more tokens than chat because every step re-reads its context.

## [What Is a Vector Database?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-vector-database/)

Published 2026-11-17. A vector database stores data as embeddings, lists of numbers that capture meaning, and finds the items whose meaning is closest to a query. This lets an AI system find a proposal about "customer churn" when the user asked about "clients leaving", even though the words differ. It is the usual index behind retrieval-augmented generation. Vector search is now a feature in many standard databases, so for most mid-size firms the question is which existing system to switch it on in, not which new product to buy.

## [What Is Account Planning?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-account-planning/)

Published 2026-11-17. Account planning is the practice of writing, and then keeping current, a plan for growing a specific existing customer. A good plan starts from the customer's goals rather than your product list, names the people on both sides, sets objectives with measures, and assigns actions to owners. Its value comes from being used in decisions every month, not from being completed once a year.

## [What Is Agent Identity and an Agent Registry?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-agent-identity/)

Published 2026-11-17. Agent identity means giving each AI agent its own identity, separate from the people who use it, with its own credentials, scoped permissions and a named human owner, so that every action can be traced to the agent and to the person who authorised it. An agent registry is the inventory of those agents: what exists, who owns it, what it can reach and whether it is still in use. Together they answer the question a security team or auditor will ask first: which agents act for this company, and on whose authority.

## [What Is Agent Memory?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-agent-memory/)

Published 2026-11-17. Agent memory is the mechanism that lets an AI agent carry information from one step, task or session to the next: facts about customers, what happened in earlier conversations, and the rules for doing a job. Short-term memory lasts for one conversation and is now built into most platforms. Long-term memory persists across sessions and is where products differ. It is useful, but it is not the same as a company's record of decisions, and it struggles most with facts that have changed.

## [What Is Agent Washing?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-agent-washing/)

Published 2026-11-17. Agent washing is the practice of rebranding existing AI assistants, chatbots or robotic process automation (RPA) tools as "agentic AI" without adding real agent capabilities. Gartner, which uses the term in its agentic AI research, estimates that only about 130 of the thousands of vendors claiming agentic products are genuine. For a buyer, the risk is paying agent prices for assistant behaviour. A short, structured demo usually exposes the difference.

## [What Is Agentic AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-agentic-ai/)

Published 2026-11-17. Agentic AI is software that pursues a goal by planning its own steps, calling tools and acting on the results, with limited human supervision. It differs from a chatbot, which answers one prompt, and from a fixed workflow, which follows steps written in advance. The category is growing fast and failing often. Teams that succeed set the level of autonomy per task and start with work that is cheap to get wrong.

## [What Is AI Governance?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-ai-governance/)

Published 2026-11-17.
