AI governance is the set of roles, policies, records and controls through which an organisation decides how it uses AI, who is accountable for each use and how risks are found and managed. Three frameworks shape most programmes: NIST's voluntary AI Risk Management Framework, the ISO/IEC 42001 management system standard, and the EU AI Act. For a 20 to 500 person company, governance starts with an inventory, named owners and a record of decisions, not a committee.

## [What Is AI Hallucination?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-ai-hallucination/)

Published 2026-11-17. AI hallucination is when a language model produces a statement that sounds plausible but is false, such as an invented figure, policy or citation. NIST calls it confabulation. It happens because models generate likely text rather than checking facts, and because standard training and testing reward a confident guess over "I don't know". It can be reduced but not eliminated, so outputs that reach clients need a person to check them.

## [What Is AI Inference Cost?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-ai-inference-cost/)

Published 2026-11-17. AI inference cost is what it costs to run a trained model each time it is used: to read a request and produce an answer. For API users it appears as a price per million input and output tokens, plus charges for caching, tools, processing tier and regional processing. For self-hosted models it is hardware, energy and staff. Unit prices have fallen fast, but agents, reasoning and long context raise the tokens used per task, so total spend often rises.

## [What Is AI Literacy, and What Does the EU AI Act Require?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-ai-literacy/)

Published 2026-11-17. AI literacy is the skills, knowledge and understanding that let people use AI systems in an informed way and see their opportunities, risks and possible harms. Article 4 of the EU AI Act requires providers and deployers to take measures that support AI literacy among their staff and others using AI on their behalf. Since the Digital Omnibus amendment took effect on 27 July 2026, the duty is one of effort: no specific level has to be guaranteed for any individual.

## [What Is AI Orchestration?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-ai-orchestration/)

Published 2026-11-17. AI orchestration is the coordination of AI models, tools, data sources and human steps so they work together as one process. It decides which model handles which step, what data each step sees, which tools can be called, and where a person approves. It ranges from fixed workflows, where code sets the path, to agents that decide their own next step. Most commercial processes are best served by the simpler end.

## [What Is AI Red Teaming?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-ai-red-teaming/)

Published 2026-11-17. AI red teaming is a structured testing exercise in which people, sometimes helped by automated tools, deliberately try to make an AI system fail: leak data, take an action it should not, produce harmful content or ignore its rules. NIST describes it as probing an AI system to find flaws and vulnerabilities. It differs from ordinary evaluation because the tester behaves like an adversary, and it is most useful when aimed at what the system can actually reach and do.

## [What Is an Agent Framework?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-agent-framework/)

Published 2026-11-17. An agent framework is software that runs agent loops for you. It calls the model, executes the tools the model asks for, keeps state between steps, pauses for a person's approval and records what happened. LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework and Google's Agent Development Kit are the best-known options. Choose one on how it handles state, approvals and tracing rather than on demos, and keep your instructions, tests and decision record outside it.

## [What Is an Agent Loop?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-agent-loop/)

Published 2026-11-17. An agent loop is the repeated cycle in which an AI model reads the current state, decides on a next step, calls a tool, observes the result and goes round again until it finishes or a limit stops it. It is what separates an agent from a single model call. The loop itself is now standard in every major agent toolkit. What differs between agents is the context that goes in and the limits placed around it.

## [What Is an AI Acceptable Use Policy?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-ai-acceptable-use-policy/)

Published 2026-11-17. An AI acceptable use policy is a short document that tells staff which AI tools they may use at work, what data they may and may not put into them, which uses need review or approval, and who to ask when unsure. It is the practical front end of AI governance. For a 20 to 500 person firm, a one-page policy with a clear data rule and a named owner does more than a long one nobody reads.

## [What Is an AI Agent, and Where Does It Fit in the Brain?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-ai-agent/)

Published 2026-11-17. An AI agent is a model working in a loop toward a goal: it chooses its next step, acts through tools, checks the result and repeats until it finishes or a limit stops it. Agents can now complete long, well-specified software tasks, and most large companies report using them, but reliability falls sharply as tasks lengthen and most production agents still hand work back to a person. They become valuable to a business when they are plugged into a company's brain: the wiring that connects its systems, the record of what it decided and why, a gate before anything leaves the building, and a path for outcomes to flow back.

## [What Is an AI Audit Trail?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-ai-audit-trail/)

Published 2026-11-17. An AI audit trail is the record that lets a firm reconstruct, after the fact, what an AI system was given, what it produced or did, which model and instructions it used, and who approved the result. In financial services it is the evidence a supervisor asks for when a client outcome is questioned. Logs from tools are part of it; the decisions, approvals and outcomes the firm records are the rest.

## [What Is an AI Autonomy Level?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-ai-autonomy-level/)

Published 2026-11-17. An AI autonomy level is a setting that states how much an AI system may do without a person: answer a question, draft work, act once approved, act and report afterwards, or act alone. It is a design decision made for each task, separate from how capable the model is. **lowob** uses a five-step dial from 0 to 4. Most commercial value today sits at levels 1 to 3, and anything that reaches a client stays at level 2 or below until there is evidence to move it.

## [What Is an AI Bill of Materials?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-ai-bill-of-materials/)

Published 2026-11-17. An AI bill of materials (AI-BOM) is a structured, usually machine-readable list of what an AI system is made of: the models and their lineage, the datasets used to train and test them, the software libraries and services they depend on, and the infrastructure they run on. It extends the software bill of materials (SBOM) that security teams already use. In May 2026, CISA and G7 partners published voluntary minimum elements for one. For most 20 to 500 person firms it is something to request from vendors, not something to produce.

## [What Is an AI Center of Excellence?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-ai-center-of-excellence/)

Published 2026-11-17. An AI center of excellence (CoE) is an internal team that sets the standards for how a company uses AI, decides which requests get built or bought first, runs pilots, and helps other teams build skills. Its purpose is to stop AI adoption from becoming either fragmented or ungoverned. Large firms staff it with data scientists, engineers and governance specialists; a 20 to 500 person firm can run one with two or three people, provided someone owns it and it has a written mandate.

## [What Is an AI Connector?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-ai-connector/)

Published 2026-11-17. An AI connector is an integration that makes one business system, such as email, a CRM or a shared drive, readable or writable by an AI assistant or agent. Some connectors copy content into an index ahead of time; others fetch it live when someone asks, increasingly through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). A good connector carries the source system's permissions with it, which makes those permissions the first thing to check. Connectors are wiring: rent them rather than build them.

## [What Is an AI Impact Assessment?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-ai-impact-assessment/)

Published 2026-11-17. An AI impact assessment is a documented review of how an AI system could affect the people and groups it touches: who is affected, what could go wrong for them, what benefits are expected and what controls apply. It is done before deployment and repeated when the system, its data or its use changes. ISO/IEC 42005 gives guidance on how to do one; the EU AI Act and the GDPR make specific versions mandatory in specific cases.

## [What Is an AI Kill Switch?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-ai-kill-switch/)

Published 2026-11-17. An AI kill switch is a control that lets a named person stop an AI agent, or every agent, immediately. It is rarely one button. It is a set of layers: pause the agent, revoke its credentials, cut its tools and cap its spending. A kill switch that has never been tested is an assumption, not a control.

## [What Is an AI SDR?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-ai-sdr/)

Published 2026-11-17. An AI SDR is an AI agent that does the work of a sales development representative: it researches target accounts, writes and sends prospecting emails, answers replies and books meetings for human sellers. Products differ mainly in how much they may do without a person. The safe starting point is to let it research and draft, and to have a person approve every message before it sends.

## [What Is an AI Agent's Time Horizon?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-ai-time-horizon/)

Published 2026-11-17. An AI agent's time horizon is the length of task, measured by how long it takes a skilled human, that the agent can complete with a stated probability, usually 50%. The measure comes from METR, an AI evaluation non-profit, which found that the 50% horizon of frontier models has doubled roughly every seven months since 2019. It is a useful signal of how fast agents are improving, and a poor guide to how much client work an agent can be trusted with unsupervised.

## [What Is an Approval Gate for AI Agents?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-approval-gate/)

Published 2026-11-17. An approval gate is a checkpoint where an AI agent pauses before a chosen action, such as sending an email or updating a price, until a named person approves, edits or rejects it. The decision and the evidence behind it are logged. In The Build Order it is Gateway 1: nothing an agent produces leaves the company until a person has approved it.

## [What Is an Enterprise Brain?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-enterprise-brain/)

Published 2026-11-17. An enterprise brain is the system that lets a company's people and AI agents act on what the company knows, has decided and has learned. It is a loop, not a product: a store of records, wiring that connects them, a record of decisions with reasons, models and agents that reason over all three, and outcomes written back. Vendors now sell parts of it under the name, but no single tool is the whole thing.

## [What Is an LLM Gateway?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-llm-gateway/)

Published 2026-11-17. An LLM gateway is a proxy that sits between a company's applications and the AI model providers they call. Every request passes through it, so the gateway can check who is calling, enforce budgets and rate limits, route to a different model if one fails, filter sensitive data and log each call. It turns many separate API keys and bills into one control point.

## [What Is an Open-Weight Model?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-open-weight-model/)

Published 2026-11-17. An open-weight model is an AI model whose trained parameters, called weights, are published so that anyone permitted by the licence can download, run and modify it on their own hardware. Open weights are not the same as open source. The Open Source Initiative's definition also requires the training code and detailed information about the training data, and many open-weight licences add conditions on use. For a business, open weights mean control over where the model runs, in exchange for running it.

## [What Is BANT, and Is It Still Useful?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-bant/)

Published 2026-11-17. BANT is a sales qualification framework that checks four things about a prospect: Budget, Authority, Need and Timeline. It is still useful as a quick screen for inbound leads and smaller, single-buyer sales. It is weak for complex B2B deals, where authority is spread across a buying group and budget is often created after the need is proven. Most teams now use it early in the funnel and switch to a fuller framework such as MEDDICC once a deal is real.

## [What Is CAC Payback?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-cac-payback/)

Published 2026-11-17. CAC payback is the number of months it takes for the gross profit from a new customer to repay the cost of acquiring that customer. The common formula is customer acquisition cost divided by monthly revenue per customer multiplied by gross margin. A shorter payback means growth ties up less cash and survives more churn. The number is only useful if the cost side includes everything spent to win the customer.

## [What Is Context Engineering?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-context-engineering/)

Published 2026-11-17. Context engineering is the practice of choosing and maintaining the information an AI model sees at each step of a task: its instructions, the documents and records retrieved for it, the results of tools it calls and the history of the conversation. It extends prompt engineering from the wording of a request to everything around it. The discipline exists because models get worse, not better, when given too much. The right few facts beat a full data dump.

## [What Is Conversation Intelligence?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-conversation-intelligence/)

Published 2026-11-17. Conversation intelligence is software that records, transcribes and analyses sales calls and meetings. It flags topics such as competitor mentions, pricing questions and next steps, and gives managers material for coaching and deal reviews. Its limits are legal as much as technical: recording needs the right consent, and in the EU, inferring employees' emotions at work is prohibited.

## [What Is CRM Data Hygiene?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-crm-data-hygiene/)

Published 2026-11-17. CRM data hygiene is the routine practice of keeping CRM records accurate, complete, unique and current. It covers preventing bad data at entry, finding and fixing errors already in the system, and measuring quality over time. It is a habit rather than a project: a single clean-up decays within months unless rules and automatic capture keep it clean.

## [What Is Customer Churn?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-customer-churn/)

Published 2026-11-17. Customer churn is the loss of customers, or of the recurring revenue they bring, over a set period. Logo churn counts the share of customers lost. Gross revenue churn counts the share of starting recurring revenue lost to cancellations and downgrades, and is 100% minus gross revenue retention. The gap between the two shows whether you are losing many small accounts or a few large ones.

## [What Is Customer Health Scoring?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-customer-health-scoring/)

Published 2026-11-17. Customer health scoring is the practice of combining several signals about an account, such as product usage, support activity, relationship strength and payment history, into a single score that indicates renewal risk or growth potential. It lets a small team decide which accounts need attention first. A score is only useful if it has been checked against what actually happened to past customers.

## [What Is Data Enrichment?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-data-enrichment/)

Published 2026-11-17. Data enrichment is the process of adding missing or more current details to CRM records from outside sources. Typical additions are company size, industry, location and technology for accounts, and job title, seniority and contact details for people. It makes records usable for routing, scoring and segmentation, but it can also overwrite good data with bad, so the setup matters as much as the provider.

## [What Is Data Residency for AI Tools?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-data-residency-for-ai/)

Published 2026-11-17. Data residency for AI tools is the ability to control the geographic location where your prompts, files, conversation history and outputs are stored, and where the model processes them. For AI the second part matters as much as the first: a vendor can store data in Europe and still run inference in another region. Residency is usually a contract or security requirement rather than a legal one, so the right choice depends on what customers, sector rules and your own data map require.

## [What Is Deal Registration?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-deal-registration/)

Published 2026-11-17. Deal registration is the process by which a partner tells a vendor about a specific sales opportunity and asks for a protected claim on it. If the vendor approves, the partner usually gets a period in which other partners, and often the vendor's own sellers, may not work the deal, and sometimes better pricing. It is the main tool for preventing channel conflict before it starts.

## [What Is Decision Precedent in AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-decision-precedent-in-ai/)

Published 2026-11-17. Decision precedent in AI means giving a model comparable past decisions, each with its reason, owner and outcome, as context when it helps with a new decision. The model's recommendation then reflects how the company has actually decided before and what happened as a result, not only general rules. In **lowob**'s model this lives in a precedent slot: a reserved part of the agent's context holding three to five comparable past decisions, including at least one that went badly. Precedent comes from the decision record. Without recorded reasons and outcomes, there is nothing useful to retrieve.

## [What Is Ecosystem-Led Growth?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-ecosystem-led-growth/)

Published 2026-11-17. Ecosystem-led growth (ELG) is a go-to-market approach in which a company uses its partners, and the customers it shares with them, to find, win and keep business. It differs from partner-led growth in one main way: the partner does not have to resell anything. The partner's customer overlap, relationships and product integrations help the company's own sellers. The term was popularised by account-mapping vendors, so its most quoted figures are vendor data and should be read that way.

## [What Is Entity Resolution?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-entity-resolution/)

Published 2026-11-17. Entity resolution is the process of deciding which records, within one system or across several, refer to the same real-world entity, such as a company or a person. It covers deduplication inside a CRM and record linkage between systems such as the CRM, billing and support. Good entity resolution sorts each pair of records into match, non-match or "needs a person to look", and keeps the history of every merge.

## [What Is Excessive Agency in AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-excessive-agency/)

Published 2026-11-17. Excessive agency is the risk that an AI system holds more tools, permissions or freedom to act than its task needs, so that a hallucination or a manipulated input turns into a damaging action. OWASP lists it as LLM06 in its 2025 Top 10 for LLM applications. It is the reason prompt injection becomes a breach rather than a bad answer, and it is fixed by scoping, not by smarter models.

## [What Is Fine-Tuning, and When Is It Worth It?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-fine-tuning/)

Published 2026-11-17. Fine-tuning is further training of an existing AI model on a set of your own examples, so it behaves more consistently on a specific task. It changes how a model responds, such as its format, tone or classification choices, more reliably than it adds new facts. Vendor guidance is to write evaluations and try prompting first, use retrieval for knowledge, and fine-tune only when those fall short. For most commercial teams it is a later step.

## [What Is Function Calling (Tool Use) in AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-function-calling/)

Published 2026-11-17. Function calling, also called tool use, is the mechanism that lets a language model ask for an action. The application tells the model which functions exist and what each one does. The model replies with a structured request naming a function and its arguments, the application runs it, and the result goes back to the model. The model never runs anything itself. Function calling is the building block under agents, connectors and MCP, and it is where permissions and approvals belong.

## [What Is Human-in-the-Loop AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-human-in-the-loop-ai/)

Published 2026-11-17. Human-in-the-loop AI is a design in which a person reviews, approves or can override an AI system's output before it takes effect. It appears in the EU AI Act's human oversight article, in UK data protection guidance and in OWASP's security mitigations. It is a real control only when the reviewer understands the output, can reject or stop it, and is measured on whether they actually check.

## [What Is Intent Data, and How Reliable Is It?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-intent-data/)

Published 2026-11-17. Intent data is behavioural evidence that an organisation is researching a topic, used to infer that it may be preparing to buy. It comes from your own channels, from partner sites and from third-party publisher networks. It is a useful timing signal at account level and a weak one at person level, so it should prioritise attention, not replace qualification.

## [What Is ISO/IEC 42001?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-iso-42001/)

Published 2026-11-17. ISO/IEC 42001 is the international standard that specifies requirements for an AI management system: the policies, roles, risk processes and records through which an organisation governs the AI it builds or uses. Unlike the NIST AI RMF, it can be certified by an accredited third party. For a mid-size company it matters most when enterprise buyers start asking for proof that AI is governed, in the way they already ask for ISO 27001 or SOC 2.

## [What Is Lead Scoring?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-lead-scoring/)

Published 2026-11-17. Lead scoring is a method of ranking leads by how likely they are to become customers, so sales and marketing work the best ones first. Most scores combine fit, meaning how closely the person and company match your ideal customer, with engagement, meaning what they have done recently. Scores work as a queue-ordering tool, provided they are checked against conversions and extended from single people to the buying group.

## [What Is Lead Source Attribution?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-lead-source-attribution/)

Published 2026-11-17. Lead source attribution is the practice of recording where each lead came from and carrying that source through to the opportunity and the revenue it produces. In most CRMs it starts as a single field holding one value, which means it captures first touch only. It answers "which channels bring us business" well enough to steer spend, provided the source list is fixed, the field is protected, and nobody mistakes it for proof of cause.

## [What Is LLM Observability?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-llm-observability/)

Published 2026-11-17. LLM observability is the practice of recording what an AI application did on every run, including the prompts, model responses, tool and retrieval steps, tokens, cost, latency and quality scores, so a team can see why it behaved as it did. Ordinary monitoring tells you a service is up. Observability for LLMs tells you whether the answer was right, what it cost and which step went wrong.

## [What Is MEDDICC?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-meddicc/)

Published 2026-11-17. MEDDICC is a sales qualification framework for complex B2B deals. The letters stand for Metrics, Economic buyer, Decision criteria, Decision process, Identify pain, Champion and Competition. Each element is a question the seller must answer with evidence from the buyer, not with an opinion. It works best when each letter becomes a field in the CRM and a condition for moving a deal to the next stage.

## [What Is Model Drift?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-model-drift/)

Published 2026-11-17. Model drift is the change in an AI system's behaviour or accuracy over time after it has been deployed. It has two broad causes. The world can change, so the data a model sees no longer resembles what it was built on. Or the model itself changes, because a provider updates or retires the version you call. Drift is caught by re-running the same tests on a schedule and comparing the results.

## [What Is Model Risk Management for AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-model-risk-management/)

Published 2026-11-17. Model risk management (MRM) is the discipline of identifying, validating, monitoring and governing the models an organisation relies on, so that a wrong or misused model does not cause financial loss or poor decisions. It grew up in banking. In April 2026 US banking agencies rescinded the long-standing SR 11-7 guidance and replaced it with shorter, risk-based guidance, SR 26-2, which leaves generative and agentic AI out of scope. Firms using AI to drive decisions still need the same core habits: an inventory, a materiality judgment, independent challenge and ongoing monitoring.

## [What Is Net Revenue Retention (NRR)?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-net-revenue-retention/)

Published 2026-11-17. Net revenue retention (NRR) is the revenue a firm earns from a group of existing customers at the end of a period, divided by what the same customers paid at the start. It includes expansion, downgrades and churn, and excludes new customers. Above 100% means the existing base grows on its own. Its companion, gross revenue retention (GRR), excludes expansion and can never exceed 100%.

## [What Is Outcome-Based Pricing for AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-outcome-based-pricing-for-ai/)

Published 2026-11-17. Outcome-based pricing for AI charges only when the AI delivers a defined result, such as a support ticket resolved without a human. It is the most attractive pricing model for buyers and the hardest to run, because everything depends on how the outcome is defined and who measures it. Customer service is where it works today. Elsewhere, it is still rare.

## [What Is Outcome Write-Back?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-outcome-write-back/)

Published 2026-11-17. Outcome write-back is the step where what actually happened after a decision is recorded against that decision, in the system the next decision will read from. It is the learning stage of the enterprise brain. Without it, agents and people see what was decided but never whether it worked, so the same mistakes repeat with more confidence each time.

## [What Is Permission-Aware Retrieval?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-permission-aware-retrieval/)

Published 2026-11-17. Permission-aware retrieval is search for AI systems that returns only the documents and records the requesting person could already open in the source system. It is the standard design for enterprise assistants and the right one. It also inherits every bad permission a company has: a pricing file shared with the whole firm was harmless while nobody could find it, and becomes visible once an assistant can. Audit permissions on commercial content before connecting it, and test with a restricted user.

## [What Is Pipeline Coverage?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-pipeline-coverage/)

Published 2026-11-17. Pipeline coverage is the value of open opportunities expected to close in a period, divided by the revenue target still to be met in that period. A ratio of 3x means there is three times as much pipeline as target. The right ratio is not a constant: it is roughly the inverse of your win rate by value, adjusted for how much of the pipeline can close in time. Coverage is only as reliable as the stage definitions and close dates behind it.

## [What Is Product-Led Growth?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-product-led-growth/)

Published 2026-11-17. Product-led growth (PLG) is a go-to-market motion in which the product does most of the work of acquiring, converting and expanding customers. People sign up, try it free or cheaply and start paying when it proves useful; sales, if there is a sales team, joins later to grow the account. It suits products that deliver value without a conversation and a buyer who can decide alone. Benchmarks suggest only a small share of free users ever pay, so the economics depend on volume and on what happens after sign-up.

## [What Is Prompt Caching?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-prompt-caching/)

Published 2026-11-17. Prompt caching is a provider feature that stores the processed form of the fixed start of a prompt, such as instructions, tool definitions or a long document, so later requests that begin the same way skip that work. Cached input is billed at a fraction of the normal rate and the response starts sooner. The answer itself is unchanged. It only works if the repeated part comes first and stays identical, so prompt design decides whether a team gets the saving.

## [What Is Prompt Engineering?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-prompt-engineering/)

Published 2026-11-17. Prompt engineering is the practice of writing, structuring and testing the instructions an AI model works from, so that its output is accurate, consistent and in the format a team needs. It covers the role, the task, the examples, the order of material and the output format. Small wording and formatting changes can move results a long way, so a prompt is only as good as the tests run against it. It is one part of context engineering, which decides everything else the model sees.

## [What Is Prompt Injection?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-prompt-injection/)

Published 2026-11-17. Prompt injection is an attack in which instructions hidden in text an AI model reads cause it to do what the attacker wants instead of what its owner intended. It ranks first in OWASP's 2025 list of risks for LLM applications. Because language models do not reliably separate instructions from data, it cannot be patched away; it has to be contained by limiting what an agent can reach and do.

## [What Is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-retrieval-augmented-generation/)

Published 2026-11-17. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique in which an AI system first searches a store of documents for passages relevant to a question, then gives those passages to a language model to write its answer. It lets a general model answer from your proposals, contracts and policies without retraining it. It reduces made-up answers but does not remove them. Most RAG failures are retrieval failures, so the quality of what goes in decides the quality of what comes out.

## [What Is Revenue Intelligence?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-revenue-intelligence/)

Published 2026-11-17. Revenue intelligence is software that captures what sellers and buyers actually do, such as emails, meetings and calls, joins it to CRM data and uses it to score deals, flag risks and support the forecast. It tests whether a deal is as healthy as the seller says. Gartner now files it within a wider market, revenue action orchestration, which adds AI assistants and agents that act on the signals.

## [What Is Revenue Operations (RevOps)?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-revenue-operations/)

Published 2026-11-17. Revenue operations (RevOps) is a single function that owns the data, processes, tools and definitions behind marketing, sales and customer success. It replaces three separate operations teams with one view of how revenue is generated and kept. Its main output is not a report but agreement: one pipeline, one set of stage definitions, one source of truth that people and AI agents can both rely on.

## [What Is Reverse ETL?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-reverse-etl/)

Published 2026-11-17. Reverse ETL is the process of copying modelled data from a data warehouse back into the operational tools a team uses, such as the CRM, the marketing platform or the support desk. It runs in the opposite direction to ordinary ETL, which loads data into the warehouse. For a commercial team it is how product usage, health scores and finance figures reach the account record where sellers, and now agents, actually read.

## [What Is Robotic Process Automation (RPA) in the Age of Agents?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-robotic-process-automation/)

Published 2026-11-17. Robotic process automation (RPA) is software that repeats a person's actions on a screen, such as clicking, typing and copying data between applications, to run rule-based tasks. It is most useful where a system has no API or connector. In the age of agents, RPA has become the dependable executor that agents and workflows call, while models handle the judgment that RPA scripts never could.

## [What Is Sales Forecasting, and Why Is It Usually Wrong?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-sales-forecasting/)

Published 2026-11-17. Sales forecasting is the practice of estimating how much revenue a team will close in a given period, usually a month or quarter. Most forecasts combine pipeline data with the judgment of sellers and managers. They are usually wrong for structural reasons: stage probabilities are guesses, close dates slip, data is incomplete, and nobody measures past error, so the same bias repeats.

## [What Is Sales Velocity?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-sales-velocity/)

Published 2026-11-17. Sales velocity is the revenue a sales pipeline produces per day. It multiplies the number of qualified opportunities by average deal size and win rate, then divides by the average sales cycle in days. The single number matters less than its four inputs: velocity shows which lever is moving, and lets a team test whether a change in one is worth a loss in another.

## [What Is Seat-Based Pricing for AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-seat-based-pricing-for-ai/)

Published 2026-11-17. Seat-based pricing charges a fixed fee for each named user of an AI tool, usually per month and often with an annual commitment. It is the standard model for AI assistants because it is easy to budget. Its weakness is that a seat measures access, not work: seats go unused, and an agent that works for many people does not fit the per-user model well.

## [What Is Selling Time, and Why Do Sellers Spend So Little of It Selling?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-seller-time-to-sell/)

Published 2026-11-17. Selling time is the share of a seller's working week spent directly engaging prospects and clients: prospecting, meetings, calls and correspondence with buyers. Large surveys put it at roughly 30% to 40% of the week. The rest goes to administration, internal coordination, data entry and searching for information, most of which can be reduced by better process before any AI tool is added.

## [What Is Shadow AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-shadow-ai/)

Published 2026-11-17. Shadow AI is the use of AI tools at work without the organisation's knowledge, approval or oversight: a personal chatbot account used for client emails, a free notetaker joining sales calls, a browser extension reading the CRM. It is usually well-meant. The risk is that company and client data flows to services nobody has assessed, and that decisions get made with tools nobody can audit.

## [What Is Structured Output in AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-structured-output/)

Published 2026-11-17. Structured output is a model feature that makes an AI response follow a fixed format, usually a JSON schema the developer supplies, so software can read it without guessing. The main providers now enforce the schema during generation, so the output parses and contains the required fields. It does not make the values correct. Structured output is how AI can write into a CRM, a queue or an approval step safely, provided the values are checked before anything acts on them.

## [What Is Synthetic Data?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-synthetic-data/)

Published 2026-11-17. Synthetic data is artificial data produced by an algorithm so that it reproduces the statistical patterns of a real dataset without copying its records. It is used to test systems, to train models where real data is scarce or sensitive, and to share data more safely. It is not automatically anonymous, and it is only as good as the real data and the method behind it.

## [What Are TAM, SAM and SOM?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-tam-sam-som/)

Published 2026-11-17. TAM, SAM and SOM are three nested estimates of market size. TAM (total addressable market) is total annual demand for a category, SAM (serviceable available market) is the part a firm can reach with its current product and channels, and SOM (serviceable obtainable market) is the share it can realistically win in a set period. For planning, the smallest number matters most, and it should be built from countable accounts rather than from an industry report.

## [What Is the Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-the-agent2agent-protocol/)

Published 2026-11-17. The Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol is an open standard that lets AI agents built by different vendors find each other, hand off tasks and report progress. Google launched it in April 2025 and transferred it to the Linux Foundation two months later. Where MCP connects one agent to tools and data, A2A connects agents to other agents. For most mid-size firms it matters first as a buying criterion, not something to build on.

## [What Is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-the-model-context-protocol/)

Published 2026-11-17. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard for connecting AI applications to the systems where data and tools live, such as a CRM, a document store or a database. Instead of building a custom integration for every pairing of AI tool and business system, each system exposes one MCP server and any MCP-compatible assistant can use it. It is now supported by most major AI products. It is wiring, not judgment, so it needs permissions and logs around it.

## [What Is the NIST AI Risk Management Framework?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-the-nist-ai-risk-management-framework/)

Published 2026-11-17. The NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) is voluntary guidance from the US National Institute of Standards and Technology for identifying and managing the risks of designing, developing, deploying and using AI. Its core is four functions: govern, map, measure and manage. It cannot be certified against and carries no legal force, but buyers, auditors and other frameworks refer to it, so it is a common language for AI risk.

## [What Is Usage-Based Pricing for AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-usage-based-pricing-for-ai/)

Published 2026-11-17. Usage-based pricing for AI charges for the volume of work the AI does, measured in tokens, conversations, actions or credits, rather than per named user. It fits agents better than seat pricing, because one agent can do the work of several people. It also makes the bill harder to predict. Buyers should accept it only with caps, estimates and alerts, and with a clear idea of what one completed task costs.

## [What Is Value-Based Pricing?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-value-based-pricing/)

Published 2026-11-17. Value-based pricing sets a price from the value an offer creates for a specific buyer, measured against that buyer's next best alternative, rather than from the seller's cost or a competitor's list price. Pricing researchers generally rank it as the strongest of the three main approaches, and the evidence says it is the least used. The arithmetic is simple. The hard parts are measuring value with real customer data and holding the price once a negotiation starts.

## [What Is Win-Loss Analysis?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-win-loss-analysis/)

Published 2026-11-17. Win-loss analysis is the structured study of why deals are won or lost, based mainly on interviews with the buyers who made the decision. It compares what buyers say with what the CRM recorded, finds patterns across deals, and feeds them back into positioning, sales process, pricing and product. Done well, it turns closed deals from outcomes into evidence.

## [What Is Zero Data Retention in AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-zero-data-retention/)

Published 2026-11-17. Zero data retention (ZDR) is an arrangement under which an AI provider does not store a customer's prompts or the model's outputs once the response has been returned. It is not a default setting: providers approve it per customer, it covers only some endpoints and features, and it keeps exceptions for content flagged by safety systems and for legal requirements. Since mid-2026 some providers have also required retention for their most capable models, so ZDR must now be checked model by model.

## [What We Would Cut From the Build Order](https://lowob.com/research/what-we-would-cut-from-the-build-order/)

Published 2026-11-17. The Build Order was written for firms of 20 to 500 people, and at the small end parts of it are too heavy. A 25-person firm does not need a formal Gateway 0, a purchased context layer, a decision-record system, a value at stake on every decision class or a Gateway 3. It needs a named owner, one decision class recorded in a shared table with outcomes, a rule that nothing sends without a person, and a handover habit that keeps the reasoning when someone leaves. The wider evidence supports cutting. RAND's study of failed AI projects names chasing the latest technology over the user's problem as one of the most frequent pathways to failure, and Anthropic's guidance on agents recommends the simplest solution possible, adding complexity only when it demonstrably improves outcomes. What should not be cut is the part that is cheapest: writing down why.

## [Which AI Assistant, Which Seats](https://lowob.com/research/which-ai-assistant-which-seats/)

Published 2026-11-17. Most firms choose an AI assistant by comparing model benchmarks, then buy seats for everyone. Both choices are usually wrong. The model is the fastest-changing layer of the stack and the least sticky; what lasts is how well the assistant fits your suite, reaches your systems, respects your controls and records what it did. And seats bought ahead of a workflow go unused. Buy for the people in the first commercial workflow, and expand on evidence.

## [Why the Brain Starts at the Commercial Line](https://lowob.com/research/why-the-brain-starts-at-the-commercial-line/)

Published 2026-11-17. Start the brain where you can count what it changed within a quarter. In most mid-size firms that is the commercial line: sales, marketing and account management. Commercial decisions recur weekly, resemble each other, show their outcome within months and have a budget holder who must defend them, and they already sit on a structured system: the CRM. The firm-wide knowledge base, the most common alternative, delivers value that is real but rarely measurable, which makes it hard to fund twice.

## [Running a Win-Loss Programme](https://lowob.com/research/win-loss-programmes/)

Published 2026-11-17. A win-loss programme is a standing process that asks buyers why they chose as they did, codes the answers against a fixed frame, and routes each recurring theme to someone who must decide what to change. The one-off study is common; the programme is rare. Gartner analyst Todd Berkowitz has argued that no more than a third of sales organisations run win-loss with rigour, and win-loss vendor Clozd reports that buyer and seller loss reasons align only 15% of the time. The fix is less about better interviews than about what happens after them: a sampling rule, a neutral interviewer, and a decision record for every finding.

## [Workflow Automation vs AI Agents: Which Do You Need?](https://lowob.com/research/workflow-automation-vs-ai-agents/)

Published 2026-11-17. Workflow automation runs a fixed sequence of steps that a person designed in advance; an AI agent is given a goal and decides its own steps and tool calls as it works. Workflows are predictable, cheap per run and easy to audit. Agents handle judgment, exceptions and unstructured inputs, at higher cost and with less predictable behaviour. Most commercial processes need a workflow with one or two model steps inside it, not an agent.

## [Your CRM Is Memory, Not a Brain](https://lowob.com/research/your-crm-is-memory-not-a-brain/)

Published 2026-11-17. A CRM is the brain's store: it holds what happened, and it does not reason about it. That makes it necessary and insufficient. Most CRM data is not ready for AI, and the risk has changed: an agent now acts on bad records automatically, before anyone reviews the decision. Before the brain can use the CRM, it needs a short set of fields kept current, a time-boxed clean-up, activity captured without typing, and a required reason for every deal that is won or lost.

## [The 10 crypto events worth the trip, Nov 2026–Jul 2027](https://lowob.com/research/the-10-crypto-events-worth-the-trip-nov-2026-jul-2027/)

Published 2026-10-26. Consensus Miami (4–6 May 2027) ranks first among crypto events worth flying to between November 2026 and July 2027, followed by Devcon 8 and EthCC[10]. The ranking reflects where deals get done for companies selling into crypto, not attendance.

## [Top 10 applied-AI events, Nov 2026–Jun 2027](https://lowob.com/research/top-10-applied-ai-events-nov-2026-jun-2027/)

Published 2026-10-26. Vendor shows are where AI roadmaps are announced, while analyst and finance-specific events are where peers in regulated firms compare what works, so a balanced year includes one of each. Gartner Data & Analytics Summit (8–10 Mar 2027, Orlando) ranks first, followed by Money20/20 Europe and AWS re:Invent.

## [Five invariants, from two people to ten thousand](https://lowob.com/research/five-invariants-from-two-people-to-ten-thousand/)

Published 2026-10-23. Almost everything about an enterprise brain changes with size: the tools, the owners, the governance, the automation, whether it can learn. Five things do not. Decisions are recorded with a reason and a falsifier; sources are kept and summaries treated as views; views are superseded, never overwritten; outcomes are written back; and the organisation owns the record. Get those right at two people and they carry you to ten thousand. Get them wrong at ten thousand and no platform will save you.

## [The 5 enterprise context platforms, ranked for regulated firms](https://lowob.com/research/the-5-enterprise-context-platforms-ranked-for-regulated-firms/)

Published 2026-10-23. Every vendor now calls this layer an "enterprise brain". What they actually sell is memory, meaning and governance: a context layer that connects a firm's documents, data and permissions to its AI agents. For a regulated firm the deciding questions are whether permissions follow the user, whether you can reconstruct what an agent saw and did, and whether you can leave with your context intact. Glean ranks first on evidence of real use across vendors, followed by Microsoft Work IQ, Google Gemini Enterprise, Writer's Enterprise Brain and Dust.

## [Top 5 AI governance and audit-trail tools](https://lowob.com/research/top-5-ai-governance-and-audit-trail-tools/)

Published 2026-10-23. AI governance platforms became a real category in 2026: Gartner published its first Magic Quadrant for them on 16 June, assessing 13 vendors. For banks and insurers they differ most on one point. Some map explicitly to model-risk guidance such as SR 26-2; most map to the EU AI Act and the NIST framework and leave bank supervision implicit. We rank IBM watsonx.governance first, ServiceNow AI Control Tower second, then Credo AI, ValidMind and ModelOp.

## [The 10 AI regulatory dates to watch through 2027](https://lowob.com/research/the-10-ai-regulatory-dates-to-watch-through-2027/)

Published 2026-10-22. The AI-specific rules keep slipping. The record-keeping, supervision and resilience rules that already apply do not. Most of what binds a bank's AI in 2027 is old law, newly read to cover agents. This list, refreshed on 16 November 2026, sets out the ten dates that change what a financial firm in the US, UK or EU must do or show, and what happened to the dates that have passed since it was first published.

## [The transitions that break the brain](https://lowob.com/research/the-transitions-that-break-the-brain/)

Published 2026-10-22. Organisations rarely lose their reasoning gradually. They lose it at transitions: the first hire, the first manager layer, an acquisition, a regulator's first visit, a founder's departure, a reorganisation, a platform migration. Each is predictable, and each has a specific defence. The failure is almost always the same: the transition is planned in terms of people, money and systems, and the reasoning is assumed to follow on its own. It does not.

## [Top 5 AI customer-service agents, by pricing model](https://lowob.com/research/top-5-ai-customer-service-agents-by-pricing-model/)

Published 2026-10-22. Customer service is the one place outcome pricing has taken hold, because a resolved ticket can be counted. That makes the definition of "resolved" the most important line in the contract. Fin and Zendesk now publish exactly what counts as a billable event; Salesforce publishes three pricing models for Agentforce; Sierra and Decagon still ask you to call sales. Fin ranks first for a published $0.99 price and the largest customer base, followed by Zendesk, Sierra, Agentforce and Decagon.

## [Top 5 AI notetakers for decision capture](https://lowob.com/research/top-5-ai-notetakers-for-decision-capture/)

Published 2026-10-21. Every notetaker now transcribes well. The difference is what happens next: whether it helps you pull out what was decided and why, whether you own and can export the record, and whether everyone on the call knew they were being recorded. Granola ranks first because it drafts notes you correct, deletes audio after transcription and exposes notes through MCP on every plan. Fireflies.ai, Fathom, Circleback and Google Meet with Gemini notes follow.

## [Top 5 tools for a founders' decision ledger](https://lowob.com/research/top-5-tools-for-a-founders-decision-ledger/)

Published 2026-10-21. None of these tools is truly append-only. Every one lets someone edit an old entry. What matters is how long the tool keeps history, whether you can get everything out in an open format, and whether it is easy enough that the weekly habit survives. Notion ranks first for flexibility and AI drafting, followed by Slite, Airtable, Obsidian and Tana. A shared document and a 30-minute weekly review beat a perfect database nobody opens.

## [Buy Context. Own Judgment. What Enterprise AI Teams Should Build](https://lowob.com/research/buy-context-own-judgment-what-to-build-at-each-size/)

Published 2026-10-20. At every size, the same rule holds: rent the context layer as it matures, and own the record of how you decide. Models, connectors, search, assistants and agent registries are products you can rent and replace. Approvals, reasoning, decision history and the ability to change vendors are what the company must control. Most firms now buy rather than build their AI, so the practical question is less "build or buy" than what to keep portable, and that answer grows with headcount.

## [The financial data providers your agents can call today](https://lowob.com/research/the-financial-data-providers-your-agents-can-call-today/)

Published 2026-10-20. In about twelve months every major financial data provider adopted the same agent connection protocol, MCP. Agents can now call licensed data from inside Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini and the cloud marketplaces. The providers differ on how much they disclose about real use, how tightly they enforce entitlements and how clearly they price. FactSet ranks first because it is the only one that has put a number on AI's share of its growth; S&P Global, LSEG, Moody's and Bloomberg follow.

## [Top 5 LLM observability and evaluation platforms](https://lowob.com/research/top-5-llm-observability-and-evaluation-platforms/)

Published 2026-10-20. The top five LLM observability and evaluation platforms for regulated teams are Langfuse, LangSmith, Arize, Braintrust and Datadog, in that order. For a regulated firm the deciding questions are whether you can host it yourself, whether it speaks the OpenTelemetry standard so you are not locked in, and whether human review is logged alongside the traces. The category consolidated hard in 2026: Humanloop is gone, Helicone is in maintenance mode and Galileo is now part of Cisco. Skip this list if you only need basic logs for a prototype.

## [Ten thousand people: density, and the case for federation](https://lowob.com/research/ten-thousand-people-density-and-the-case-for-federation/)

Published 2026-10-19. At ten thousand people, there is finally enough volume in enough decision classes for a learning layer to earn its keep. The challenge is no longer whether to record judgment, but how one organisation runs many records without forcing them into one. The tempting answer is a single enterprise brain with one ontology. The workable design is federated: invariants set centrally, records kept locally by the functions, and a map between local and enterprise definitions. Map, do not unify.

## [The 5 agent memory layers worth testing, and how to test them](https://lowob.com/research/the-5-agent-memory-layers-worth-testing-and-how-to-test-them/)

Published 2026-10-19. No memory layer has yet shown, under independent test, that it makes agents better at long tasks. The best independent benchmark we found tested how well memory systems handle a fact that has changed, and every method scored poorly when the answer needed more than one step of reasoning. Vendor scores in the 90s are real results on the vendors' own harnesses, not independent reproductions. So this is a list of what is worth testing, with a protocol for testing it, not a list of what works. Zep ranks first because its graph records when a fact stopped being true instead of overwriting it.

## [Top 5 agent frameworks for production, by state model and cloud](https://lowob.com/research/top-5-agent-frameworks-for-production-by-state-model-and-cloud/)

Published 2026-10-19. Framework choice in 2026 is mostly a cloud and vendor decision, not a technical one. The serious options all connect to tools through the same protocol, MCP, so what separates them for a regulated team is narrower: whether a run can pause at a named step for a person, resume after a crash without losing state, and run on more than one model. On those tests LangGraph ranks first, followed by Microsoft Agent Framework, the Claude Agent SDK, Google's Agent Development Kit and the OpenAI Agents SDK.

## [One thousand people: governance arrives](https://lowob.com/research/one-thousand-people-governance-arrives/)

Published 2026-10-15. At around a thousand people, auditors, regulators, security teams and large customers start asking how decisions were made, and "we discussed it" stops being an answer. The enterprise brain's job becomes governance. Four things have to exist: a trace specification for each AI-assisted decision class, a review gate that leaves evidence, registered agents with owners and scoped permissions, and retention rules agreed with counsel. The risk becomes a platform that nobody in the business owns.

## [The Enterprise Brain Is a Record, Not a Mind](https://lowob.com/research/the-enterprise-brain-is-a-record-not-a-mind/)

Published 2026-10-15. An enterprise brain is an accountable record that people and AI agents read before they act and write to afterwards, not a mind that thinks for the company. Products sold under the name supply memory, meaning and governance well. They do not supply the fourth requirement, judgment: a dated record of what the company decided, why, who approved it, what it replaced and whether it worked. Agent memory research agrees: agents usually fail after the evidence is found, when they must work out which version is current.

## [Two hundred people: reasoning that travels without its author](https://lowob.com/research/two-hundred-people-reasoning-that-travels-without-its-author/)

Published 2026-10-14. At a few hundred people, founders make a small fraction of the decisions. Managers make most of them, many managers have never met the people whose decisions they inherit, and turnover becomes constant. The enterprise brain's job becomes delegation: letting good reasoning travel. Four things do that: formal decision classes, a precedent slot before each decision, a standard handover pack, and a first calibration in one high-volume class. The trap is compliance theatre.

## [Fifty people: when words start to mean different things](https://lowob.com/research/fifty-people-when-words-start-to-mean-different-things/)

Published 2026-10-12. At around fifty people, teams form and vocabularies drift. Sales, product and finance use the same words for different things, and AI tools amplify the confusion. The enterprise brain's job becomes meaning: shared definitions, clear decision rights, and one place where records live. Large organisations eventually build semantic layers and ontologies for this. A fifty-person company does not need either. It needs the lightweight version.

## [Ten people: the first stranger](https://lowob.com/research/ten-people-the-first-stranger/)

Published 2026-10-09. Somewhere between the third and the tenth hire, the company gains people who were not there when anything was decided. The enterprise brain's job becomes answering "why do we do it this way?" without a founder in the room. The founders' ledger stays, rewritten so strangers can read it, with three additions: short "why we do it this way" pages, a handful of first definitions with owners, and onboarding through the record. The trap is a topic wiki.

## [Raise, Rally, Revenue: the whole series on one page](https://lowob.com/research/raise-rally-revenue/)

Published 2026-10-07. Fundraising, community and customers are one system, not three projects, and it runs in a fixed order: name the buyer, write one truth, collect evidence, raise against it, give the community a job, make first customers design partners, distribute, measure, then hand over. Every failure in the series came from doing a right thing at the wrong time. The 2026 data makes the order harder to skip: venture capital is concentrated in a few very large rounds, enterprise buyers are funding new tools from new budgets, and platforms are sending publishers and brands less traffic than they did.

## [Two people: the founders' ledger](https://lowob.com/research/two-people-the-founders-ledger/)

Published 2026-10-07. At two people, the enterprise brain is a single document and a weekly habit. Its job is to stop two honest people remembering the same decision differently, and it is worth more than any tool you could buy at this stage. One append-only ledger, one line per material decision with its reason, what was rejected, what would prove it wrong and where the founders disagreed, reviewed for 30 minutes a week.

## [The scale ladder](https://lowob.com/research/the-scale-ladder/)

Published 2026-10-06. There is no single right enterprise brain. There is a right one for two people, a different one for fifty, and a very different one for 10,000. What changes as an organisation grows is not whether it needs a record of its judgment, but which problem that record has to solve: false shared memory at two people, the first stranger at ten, meaning at fifty, delegation at two hundred, governance at a thousand and density at ten thousand. The mistake at every size is building the brain of the wrong stage. The rule is to build for the next rung, not two rungs up.

## [Built to be kept without us](https://lowob.com/research/built-to-be-kept-without-us/)

Published 2026-10-02. The honest test of any judgment system, and of anyone who installs one, is whether it keeps working after they leave. A system whose operators cannot be removed without the record degrading has the same flaw it was built to fix. Regulators now treat switching barriers as a market failure: the EU Data Act bans cloud switching charges from January 2027, and the UK's competition authority found egress fees and interoperability barriers limit customer choice. Those rules help you leave a vendor. They do not make a record readable without the people who built it, which is the harder test.

## [Handovers are where reasoning pours out](https://lowob.com/research/handovers-are-where-reasoning-pours-out/)

Published 2026-10-01. Reasons leak from organisations all the time. At handovers they pour out, all at once, on a date everyone knows in advance. The standard handover transfers files, logins and a status list, which is what was already written down, and loses the reasoning, which was not. A five-part pack started four weeks before departure keeps it: extracted decisions, open threads, relationships, a graveyard of abandoned approaches, and a question log for the first 90 days. For an organisation with no judgment record, it is the cheapest place to start one.

## [The Agency You Hired Spent $50K. What Did You Actually Get?](https://lowob.com/research/the-agency-spent-50k-and-i-have-nothing-to-point-at/)

Published 2026-10-01. A company can spend $50,000 on marketing, receive every promised campaign and report, and still be unable to say whether the work attracted a single valuable customer. That is not necessarily evidence that the agency is dishonest or ineffective. It usually means the money went out before anyone agreed what success would look like, who owned the accounts, or how results would be measured. Buyers are noticing: 39% of marketing leaders in Gartner's 2025 survey planned to cut agency budgets. Separate what the money bought, get the accounts and data back, agree what counts as a result, and only then decide whether to change agencies.

## [Below the volume floor](https://lowob.com/research/below-the-volume-floor/)

Published 2026-09-29. At 150 decisions a year, all different, no model will learn your judgment, and pooling across companies does not rescue it. The arithmetic is unforgiving: split 150 decisions across ten classes and a calibration curve needs years per class to stabilise. What still works is narrower and still valuable: your own prior reasoning, recorded properly, plus public base rates, read and argued with by a person. Forecasting research supports starting from the base rate.

## [Reviewer minutes per useful decision](https://lowob.com/research/reviewer-minutes-per-useful-decision/)

Published 2026-09-28. Token costs get the attention. The number that decides whether a judgment system pays for itself is human review time per decision that actually helped. Expect it to rise before it falls: economists call the pattern a productivity J-curve, and it is where most programmes lose their sponsor. Measure the baseline, predict the peak, put the crossover date in writing, and treat a miss as a decision.

## [The humans carrying context are the price signal](https://lowob.com/research/the-humans-carrying-context-are-the-price-signal/)

Published 2026-09-24. Enterprises are paying expensive people to carry the context their software cannot hold. Forward-deployed engineers, embedded consultants and integration teams spend most of their time on how a particular client's world works, not on models. That spending is the clearest market price for the missing layer, and the clearest specification of what it should contain. The practical move is not to remove the people but to make sure their context does not leave with them.

## ["We shipped everything and the number went down"](https://lowob.com/research/we-shipped-everything-and-the-number-went-down/)

Published 2026-09-24. The product is proven and the number still fell, so the problem has moved to distribution; stop building, name one story, and work one channel. Shipping more is rarely the fix. Pendo's analysis of 615 software products found 80% of features were rarely or never used, and at Microsoft only about a third of tested ideas improved the metric they targeted. Supply went up. Demand did not follow, because nobody was working demand.

## [Whoever holds the record holds the company](https://lowob.com/research/whoever-holds-the-record-holds-the-company/)

Published 2026-09-23. The layer that encodes how a business decides is the deepest lock-in in enterprise software. It is also where the strongest growth is: Gartner now advises software vendors to "capture and retain customer-specific knowledge, not just data" as agents erode the value of their interfaces. Data can be exported and models are rented and switched. The accumulated record of how the organisation decides is the asset at stake. The enterprise should own it, and the contract should say so before the first workflow moves in.

## [A reviewer who does not verify is not a control](https://lowob.com/research/a-reviewer-who-does-not-verify-is-not-a-control/)

Published 2026-09-21. Human-in-the-loop is a design pattern, not a defence. Courts, regulators and clients now look for evidence that the human actually checked, and a review box on a process diagram is not that evidence. By late July 2026 one tracked database held 1,240 reported US court filings with AI-fabricated content, hundreds of them signed by lawyers. Design the review gate so that proof of verification is a by-product: sources one click away, a log of what the reviewer opened, edit classes, blind second looks and seeded errors.

## ["40,000 members and nobody does anything"](https://lowob.com/research/40-000-members-and-nobody-does-anything/)

Published 2026-09-18. A large, silent community was recruited for a payout and never given a job. Pick one job, recruit thirty people by name, ask for judgment, close the loop, and count who stays when the incentives stop. Some silence is normal: most people in any online group read without posting. But a group of 40,000 where nobody acts has a design problem, not a participation problem.

## [Regulators want the chain, not the model](https://lowob.com/research/regulators-want-the-chain-not-the-model/)

Published 2026-09-18. Financial supervisors are not asking to inspect your model. They are asking you to reconstruct what it did, step by step, and who checked. FINRA's 2026 oversight report asks firms to track agent actions and decisions; the FCA's October 2026 review praises firms that kept records of prompts, outputs, model versions and escalation decisions; US bank supervisors have been asking whether banks can audit what their agents decide; and the EU AI Act requires high-risk systems to log events automatically. That trace is the same object a judgment system needs in order to learn. Build it once, as the spine of the product.

## [Where judgment arrives first](https://lowob.com/research/where-judgment-arrives-first/)

Published 2026-09-16. Judgment layers will work first where decisions are frequent, similar and graded quickly, and where someone will later have to defend them. Research on expertise says the same thing about people: skilled judgment is learnable only where the environment is regular and feedback arrives. Map your decision classes on volume and outcome lag before choosing where to build. Everywhere else, judgment is a practice before it is a product.

## [The graveyard](https://lowob.com/research/the-graveyard/)

Published 2026-09-15. The most valuable thing an organisation knows is what it tried and abandoned, and why. It is also the first thing lost when people move. A judgment system should make the graveyard first-class, and distinguish what was disproven from what was merely under-tried. The research supports both halves: knowledge built through work depreciates quickly, and NASA's own inspector general found that only 57% of project managers surveyed used the agency's lessons-learned system at all.

## [Approval rate measures fatigue too](https://lowob.com/research/approval-rate-measures-fatigue-too/)

Published 2026-09-11. "Accepted without edit" rises when an AI system improves. It also rises when reviewers get tired, trust fluent text, stop seeing hard cases, or ask for less. Read alone, the number cannot tell these apart, and the people producing it cannot either: experienced developers in a 2025 randomised trial were 19% slower with AI and believed they were 20% faster. A few cheap measures can separate improvement from fatigue. Report approval rate beside them or not at all.

## ["The round has stalled"](https://lowob.com/research/the-round-has-stalled/)

Published 2026-09-11. A stalled round is a process fault or an evidence gap, and the pass reasons tell you which. Read them, fix the gap or pause, then compress what is left into two weeks. Stalls are more common in 2026 than the headline numbers suggest: deals under $100 million took only 12.5% of US venture dollars in the first half of the year, and seed capital on Carta's platform fell by almost half, so many companies are competing for a smaller pool.

## [Dissent is the data you are throwing away](https://lowob.com/research/dissent-is-the-data-you-are-throwing-away/)

Published 2026-09-10. When a committee decides, the minority view is smoothed out of the record. Over time, recorded dissent is often the most predictive signal an organisation has, and it costs one line to keep. Four decades of group research explain why it disappears: discussion favours what everyone already knows, members follow the most senior voice, and role-played objections carry less weight than real ones. Capture views before discussion, attribute them, attach a probability, and check them against outcomes.

## [Calibration is the honest learning signal](https://lowob.com/research/calibration-is-the-honest-learning-signal/)

Published 2026-09-08. A system cannot claim to learn by grading its own outputs. It can by comparing human predictions with outcomes it did not produce. Someone records a probability before a decision; the world produces a result; the gap is information nobody can game afterwards. Rating agencies have published this kind of scorecard for decades, and the largest forecasting experiments show calibration can be trained. Almost no other business function does it at all, and it costs one number per decision.

## [The field that makes a record a judgment](https://lowob.com/research/the-field-that-makes-a-record-a-judgment/)

Published 2026-09-07. A decision record without a stated falsifier is a press release. The one field that turns it into judgment is "what would prove this wrong, by when". A good falsifier names a measure, a threshold, a date and an observer, which turns a decision into a prediction that someone other than the author can grade. It is also the field that reveals, at the moment of decision, whether the people agreeing actually agree.

## ["The story isn't landing"](https://lowob.com/research/the-story-isnt-landing/)

Published 2026-09-07. When the story isn't landing, the deck is usually aimed at the wrong audience, built on a category word instead of a buyer, or hiding its evidence too late. Fix those three before touching anything else. The reading conditions make the third fault the most expensive: DocSend's platform data showed average seed-deck viewing time falling below two minutes in 2023, while time on traction slides rose. Three afternoon fixes, done in order, usually change the questions investors ask within two meetings.

## [Discord Is Not a Community Strategy. Neither Is Telegram.](https://lowob.com/research/discord-telegram-community-strategy/)

Published 2026-09-05. A Discord server or Telegram group is infrastructure, not a strategy. Start from the jobs members need done, decide which need real-time chat and which need durable documentation, and build the smallest set of spaces that serves them. In crypto, safety is part of the design: the FBI recorded $11.4 billion in crypto-related fraud losses in 2025, and a chat full of impersonators is where much of it starts. Choose the platform after the behaviour.

## [The Modular GTM Team: Specialist Depth Without a Full-Service Agency](https://lowob.com/research/the-modular-gtm-team/)

Published 2026-09-04. AI and Web3 companies often need strong specialists for specific periods, without needing every specialist on payroll. A modular GTM team keeps a small group accountable for the strategy and brings in focused support when the work requires it. The pattern is not new at the top of the market: in the ANA's 2023 survey, large advertisers' in-house teams handled an average of 61% of company work, and the work that went outside went mainly for capacity or specialist skills. What makes the model work is not the roster. It is one team that stays accountable for the outcome.

## [Keep the sources; let the summary regenerate](https://lowob.com/research/keep-the-sources-let-the-summary-regenerate/)

Published 2026-09-03. A generated summary must never be the only surviving copy of a decision. Every summary is a lossy compression made by one model on one day, and research shows what gets lost: a 2025 study found model summaries of scientific papers were nearly five times more likely than expert summaries to turn hedged findings into broad generalisations. Provenance is the asset. The summary is a view. Keep immutable sources, version every summary with the model and prompt that made it, and regenerate when models improve.

## [The false premise is the expensive failure](https://lowob.com/research/the-false-premise-is-the-expensive-failure/)

Published 2026-09-02. AI systems have become good at saying "I don't know". They remain bad at saying "that's not right any more". In one 2026 benchmark, a widely used memory layer declined to answer 99.3% of questions about facts it had never seen, but resolved only 14.6% of prompts whose premise contradicted what it remembered. The second failure is the one that costs money. The fix is a premise check against the record, run on questions tied to live decisions and tested on your own reversed views.

## [How to Run a Marketing RFP Without Wasting a Quarter](https://lowob.com/research/how-to-run-a-marketing-rfp/)

Published 2026-09-01. A long agency RFP often rewards polished proposals rather than the team most likely to solve the problem, and it costs more than most buyers realise. The ANA and 4A's estimated in 2023 that a typical US agency review with three finalists costs about $1 million across the client and the agencies, and the European agency association found the average agency spends about €43,800 on each new-business pitch. A good RFP describes the real situation and outcome, asks for approach and evidence rather than free work, and weights category experience and incentives over polish. For most companies below enterprise scale, a short brief, a few conversations and a paid first engagement find the partner faster.

## [A Distribution Plan for a Product the Platforms Restrict: One Fintech Company, Ninety Days.](https://lowob.com/research/restricted-category-distribution-worked-example/)

Published 2026-09-01. This is the restricted-category method applied to one composite company: a consumer fintech app with a yield-bearing account through a partner bank, two ad accounts rejected and a budget sitting unspent. Over ninety days it maps the bands from the platforms' own policies, spends $14,000 testing three open channels against written thresholds, builds the one that read, and adds the rest in proportion. At day ninety no channel carries more than half of funded accounts, finance can reconcile the cost per funded account, and nothing required getting past a review.

## [AI Is Making Execution Cheap. Judgment Is Becoming the Marketing Moat.](https://lowob.com/research/judgment-is-the-moat/)

Published 2026-08-31. A team can now produce a month's worth of posts, landing-page drafts and campaign ideas in an afternoon. If nobody has decided who the work is for or what it needs to accomplish, faster production does not solve much. In the Content Marketing Institute's 2026 survey, 88% of B2B marketers said their organisation uses AI content tools and 65% faced more pressure to produce content faster. When everyone can produce, knowing what is worth publishing, and checking whether it worked, is the advantage.

## [Revenue models for long cycles](https://lowob.com/research/revenue-models-for-long-cycles/)

Published 2026-08-31. Pick the revenue model by who carries the capital and the service tail, price pilots and production differently, and report only what would survive due diligence. The revenue model also decides how the company is financed. US federal energy lenders, for example, prefer technology at readiness level 8, deny pilot and demonstration projects and look for contracted cash flows, so the contract terms you write today decide whether your fiftieth unit is funded by debt or by more dilution.

## [Supersede, never overwrite](https://lowob.com/research/supersede-never-overwrite/)

Published 2026-08-31. Finance already knows how to store what was true and when it was known. Apply the same discipline to beliefs. A memory that edits itself in place cannot explain itself, and the change is the information. Judgment records should carry two dates, when a view was valid and when the organisation held it, and a changed view should be a new record linked to the old one by an explicit supersession, with a date, an author, a reason and a trigger.

## [Retrieval is not the bottleneck](https://lowob.com/research/retrieval-is-not-the-bottleneck/)

Published 2026-08-28. The right evidence is usually there. Memory systems fail at weighing and applying it, especially when it has changed. A June 2026 benchmark found that when memory systems failed, the relevant evidence was retrievable about ten times more often than it was missing, and that questions about how a fact changed were the weakest category. Better search will not fix that. Giving every piece of evidence a standing, with status, validity dates, provenance and links to what it replaced, will.

## [From Hype to Revenue: Web3's Next Competitive Advantage Is Operating Discipline](https://lowob.com/research/from-hype-to-revenue/)

Published 2026-08-27. Web3 has never had much trouble generating attention. Converting that attention into a durable business model has always been the challenge.
