The evidence on incentive-led launches shows attention fading fast: Keyrock found most of 62 airdropped tokens fell within 15 days. Meanwhile the SEC's 2026 crypto offering proposal would ask issuers for principles-based disclosure, including token economics, and for GAAP financial statements in larger raises. Hype is not the problem. Hype that goes nowhere is.

## [What Thought Leadership Actually Is](https://lowob.com/research/what-thought-leadership-actually-is/)

Published 2026-08-27. Thought leadership is a defensible position, supported by evidence the audience could not assemble, with a consequence for the reader, sustained over time. Buyers say it matters: in the 2026 Edelman-LinkedIn study, 73% of B2B decision makers said useful data or evidence is what makes thought leadership worth sharing, and 59% of final decision makers said poor or absent thought leadership had led to a vendor being dropped. Most of what carries the name is agreeable content measured by impressions. The real thing comes from a founder's or senior operator's actual thinking, on a cadence they can sustain.

## [The reason nobody types](https://lowob.com/research/the-reason-nobody-types/)

Published 2026-08-26. The operative reason for many decisions is political, personal, embarrassing or legally sensitive. A system that only records the sayable reason produces clean, coherent and quietly false records, and precedent built on them misleads. Research on organisational silence and psychological safety explains why people withhold, and Gary Klein's premortem shows that changing the frame of a question changes what people will say. No design fully fixes this, but a completeness flag, scoped visibility, a cynic's question and outcome write-back make it much better.

## [Ask for the gap, not the summary](https://lowob.com/research/ask-for-the-gap-not-the-summary/)

Published 2026-08-25. A good judgment system does not ask people to tell it everything. It knows what the next decision will need, notices what it is missing, and asks for exactly that, of the person most likely to know. The method is simple: write a needs template for each decision class, compare the live record against it, rank the gaps, and ask only the top one. One sharp question is answered in seconds. Five are an interrogation, and the research on alert fatigue shows what people do with too many prompts.

## [Integrators, OEMs and channel partners](https://lowob.com/research/integrators-oems-and-channel-partners/)

Published 2026-08-25. In emerging tech the buyer already trusts someone else's hands; your job is to make those hands want to carry you, one partner at a time. Most technology spending already moves that way: Canalys estimated 70% of customer spending on technology, IT services and telecom services would go through partners in 2025. Do the first deployments yourself, productise the playbook into documents a partner can use, then work one partner's live deal to paid pilot before adding a second. Measure partner-sourced pipeline that reaches paid pilot, and nothing else.

## [Web3 Does Not Have One Customer. That Is Why Most Launch Plans Break.](https://lowob.com/research/web3-multi-audience-launch-plan/)

Published 2026-08-25. A Web3 product can attract thousands of people to a launch announcement and still have almost nobody using it a month later, because it reached an audience but not the people needed to make it work. A protocol may need users, developers, capital providers, distribution partners, institutions and governance participants, each waiting for evidence from someone else. Map those groups, launch in the order the dependencies require, keep one product truth explained differently for each, and measure participation rather than attention.

## [Intent, not a destination](https://lowob.com/research/intent-not-a-destination/)

Published 2026-08-21. Every interaction a judgment system records should serve an explicit outcome. But naming the conclusion in advance bends the reasoning to reach it. Anthropic's research found five leading assistants consistently tailored answers to the user's stated view, and a 2023 study found biased prompts cut model accuracy by up to 36% while the explanations never mentioned the bias. The craft is keeping the purpose fixed and the answer open: name the decision, ask in a fixed schema, and run any case for something beside the case against.

## [What Makes a Case Study Believable](https://lowob.com/research/what-makes-a-case-study-believable/)

Published 2026-08-21. A prospective customer reads your case study to learn one thing: have you solved a problem like mine, and can you show me what happened? A logo, a polished testimonial and a large percentage will not answer that on their own. A believable case study reads like an account of a project: the starting situation, the decisions made, what changed with a baseline and a date, and what the evidence cannot support. Research on reviews suggests a little visible imperfection raises trust, and in the US, the FTC treats claims made through testimonials as claims the advertiser must substantiate.

## [Clipping Is Not a Fad. It Is Paid Distribution With a Human Face.](https://lowob.com/research/clipping-paid-distribution/)

Published 2026-08-20. A clipping programme pays people, usually per thousand views, to cut long-form content into short-form video and post it on their own accounts. Digiday reported typical rates of $1 to $5 per thousand views, capped per campaign. Treat it as a fad and it will look like one. Treat it as paid distribution bought at a rate per view and executed by hundreds of small publishers, and it becomes a channel with a price, a yield and a set of controls. Disclosure rules apply to every paid clip, whoever posts it.

## [The trade must clear on the spot](https://lowob.com/research/the-trade-must-clear-on-the-spot/)

Published 2026-08-20. People share what they know when they get something back in the same moment. A promise of future collective value is a public-goods problem, and public goods are under-supplied: organisational researchers have described knowledge sharing as a social dilemma since at least 2002. The smartest capture designs are two-way. The system gives the person something useful at the moment of work and takes their knowledge in return, and both halves land in the same interaction. Make the return private, immediate and visible.

## [First customers in a market that doesn't exist yet](https://lowob.com/research/first-customers-in-a-market-that-doesnt-exist-yet/)

Published 2026-08-19. In a market that does not exist yet, first customers are chosen as design partners and references at once, bought through institutional procurement, reached through practitioner networks, and measured by risk retired. The institutions that buy first are slow for reasons that can be mapped in advance: procurement thresholds, security review, liability terms and planning calendars. Sandboxes and standards bodies are distribution as well as compliance, but they are selective: the UK Financial Conduct Authority accepted 14 of 142 sandbox applications in its 2025/26 financial year.

## [A loop with good context](https://lowob.com/research/a-loop-with-good-context/)

Published 2026-08-18. An agent is a loop. The engineering that matters has moved from what you ask to what the loop knows when it asks. Research on long inputs shows that adding more context makes models less reliable, so every serious team ends up choosing what enters. The most valuable context almost nobody supplies is prior judgment on comparable cases: a precedent slot of three to five past decisions, each with its reason, outcome and any dissent, filled before the task runs and tested blind against the current version.

## [Community Management vs Social Media Management](https://lowob.com/research/community-vs-social-media-management/)

Published 2026-08-18. Social media management is editorial work: the company's voice on its own accounts, measured by reach, response and traffic. Community management is hosting work: members' voices in spaces the company runs, measured by returning members and how much they help each other. Job descriptions routinely merge the two, and the evidence suggests the merged role is already stretched: CMX's 2025 survey found around 30% of community teams are one person. When one person holds both, the job that gets done depends on their temperament, not the company's needs.

## [The first two-fifths](https://lowob.com/research/the-first-two-fifths/)

Published 2026-08-17. What has shipped as an "enterprise brain" is the context layer. It is the easy two-fifths of the idea, and it is the part being paid for. Data owners sell knowledge into other firms' agents, software incumbents sell governance, and meaning is being built in a few places. Memory is arriving as a feature but, on the benchmarks, does not yet track how facts change. Judgment is skipped. The missing pieces share one root cause: nothing in the stack writes an outcome back to a decision.

## [KOL Campaigns Need More Than Impression Screenshots](https://lowob.com/research/web3-kol-campaign-measurement/)

Published 2026-08-16. An impression screenshot proves a post was delivered. It does not prove anyone understood the product, connected a wallet or came back. Buy a defined behaviour, not a follower count; instrument the path from click to on-chain action before the campaign starts; judge each creator on distribution, activation, durability and economics; and make the second payment conditional on evidence. Disclosure belongs in the same brief: the FTC, the SEC, the UK FCA and MiCA all treat a paid crypto post as advertising.

## [Raising for long cycles](https://lowob.com/research/raising-for-long-cycles/)

Published 2026-08-12. Long-cycle companies raise against milestones, not time. Build a capital stack that mixes dilutive, non-dilutive, strategic and project money, and show investors one retired risk per round. The 2026 data supports the approach: hardware funding on Carta's platform nearly doubled in the first half of the year, but non-dilutive programmes proved slow and conditional, and US project lenders say plainly that they will not fund pilots.

## [Event, Newsletter, and Podcast Sponsorships Explained](https://lowob.com/research/sponsorships-events-newsletters-podcasts/)

Published 2026-08-12. Sponsorships buy the trust of an audience someone else assembled. Pay for access and explanation rather than visibility, check the property's real numbers, track with codes and links, and define the observable outcome before signing. The formats are mainstream: US podcast advertising reached $2.9 billion in 2025 according to the IAB and PwC, and Edison Research estimates 58% of Americans aged 12 and over consumed a podcast in the past month. The numbers each property reports, downloads and opens especially, need checking before they set a price.

## [The Channels Nobody Can Take Away From You Are the Ones You Keep Neglecting.](https://lowob.com/research/owned-channels-email-content/)

Published 2026-08-10. Owned channels are the ones where a company holds the relationship directly and no third party can revoke it: email, content on property it controls, the search presence that content earns, and the product's own messages. They are slow and do not look like marketing, so most companies neglect them, which is exactly why they are thinly bid. Rented channels keep changing: Chartbeat data show Facebook referrals to news sites down 43% and Google search referrals down 33% in a year. Build email first, give every piece of content a job, and connect every rented channel to an address the company keeps.

## [Founder, Brand and Community Accounts Need Different Jobs](https://lowob.com/research/founder-brand-community-social-strategy/)

Published 2026-08-07. When a founder, company and community account all repeat the same announcement, people have fewer reasons to follow each one. Give every account a distinct purpose. A founder, a company and a community have different sources of authority: the founder's is judgment, the company's is proof, the community's is participation. Trust data supports separating them. The 2026 Edelman Trust Barometer found 66% of employees trust their own CEO, and the Reuters Institute found 27% of people get news from creators and personalities, so a person and an institution are trusted for different things.

## [How to Read a Creator Media Kit](https://lowob.com/research/how-to-read-a-creator-media-kit/)

Published 2026-08-07. A creator media kit is a sales document prepared by the seller. Read past the follower count to median engagement, real demographics and repeat sponsors, ask for the numbers it leaves out, and test on cost-per-outcome terms before buying a package. Buyers have reason to be careful: a third of US creator ad buyers told the IAB in 2025 that finding the right creators was their biggest hurdle, and the US Federal Trade Commission now bans buying or selling fake follower and view counts used to misrepresent influence.

## [Selling what nobody has a budget line for](https://lowob.com/research/selling-what-nobody-has-a-budget-line-for/)

Published 2026-08-06. When no budget line exists, you sell against the cost of what the buyer does today, through a category they already recognise, to the person who owns the pain. The category story is for investors. The evidence on lost deals supports this: Matthew Dixon and Ted McKenna's analysis of 2.5 million recorded sales conversations found 40% to 60% of lost deals ended in no decision. In emerging technology, the status quo is the competitor you lose to most.

## [What Is UGC, and Why Brands Now Pay for It](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-ugc/)

Published 2026-08-03. UGC now means two things: genuine customer content, credible because it was not commissioned, and paid creator content styled to look organic, which performs in paid social. Use both, keep them distinct, and disclose and review the paid kind as the advertising it is. The rules are specific. The FTC's Endorsement Guides say ads that present people as actual consumers should use actual consumers or say otherwise, and its 2024 rule bans testimonials from people who never used the product.

## [In Emerging Tech, the Only Strategy Question Is Which Bets You Can Take Back.](https://lowob.com/research/emerging-tech-reversible-bets/)

Published 2026-08-02. Companies in emerging categories are told two contradictory things: move fast, because the window is closing, and be careful, because the rules are still being written. Both are true. The way to hold them together is not a balance between speed and caution. It is a sorting rule: which decisions can be taken back, and which cannot. Reversible decisions should be made quickly, cheaply and in parallel. Irreversible ones should be made slowly, one at a time, after the reversible ones have produced evidence.

## [From reach to recurring](https://lowob.com/research/from-reach-to-recurring/)

Published 2026-07-30. Reach is rented, recurring is owned. The move is from traffic-dependent revenue to products people pay for repeatedly, measured by conversion, churn, revenue per subscriber and platform independence. The pressure is measurable: Chartbeat data cited by the Reuters Institute shows Google organic search traffic to more than 2,500 publisher sites fell 33% globally between November 2024 and November 2025, and Pew found people clicked a search result on 8% of visits that showed an AI summary, against 15% without one.

## [Your Customers Already Wrote Your Messaging. Claude Can Help You Find It.](https://lowob.com/research/claude-voice-of-customer-research/)

Published 2026-07-29. Most companies write messaging from the inside out, and sales then discovers that buyers use different language for the problem. The strongest messaging is recovered from the market. Claude is useful as a qualitative research layer across calls, tickets, reviews and lost-deal notes, provided the team uses a disciplined method: extract fields with quoted excerpts before summarising, cluster by buying situation, and compare customer language with the company's own. A 2024 study found GPT-4 matched human coders on explicit themes but fell short on interpretive ones, which is why every finding needs its quote.

## [What Is App Store Optimization? Fintech and Crypto Apps](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-app-store-optimization/)

Published 2026-07-29. App store optimization, ASO, is the practice of improving how an app is found and chosen in the app stores: its ranking in store search, its conversion from store page to install, and its eligibility for featuring. Apple says nearly 65% of App Store downloads happen directly after a search. For fintech and crypto apps that cannot buy installs freely, the store is open-band distribution every other channel depends on, and store review is a constraint to plan around, so the listing is the channel.

## [What Is Marketing Mix Modeling? A Small-Company Guide](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-marketing-mix-modeling/)

Published 2026-07-24. Marketing mix modeling (MMM) is a statistical method that estimates how much each marketing channel, and other factors such as price and seasonality, contributed to an outcome. It works from aggregate weekly data and does not track any individual, which is why it has returned as individual tracking has declined. Google's Meridian and Meta's Robyn have made the software free. Both are clear about what it needs: history, real variation in spend, and experiments to calibrate it. The results are rough, and combined with attribution and incrementality tests they are the most honest picture a company can assemble.

## [Your first ten sponsors are design partners](https://lowob.com/research/your-first-ten-sponsors-are-design-partners/)

Published 2026-07-24. Sponsorship, data and research are B2B sales; treat the first ten buyers as design partners, agree the test and the report before the money, and measure renewal from day one. Buyers are ready for that framing. In the IAB's 2025 study of US creator ad buyers, 40% ranked overall return on investment as their top measure, and the most requested improvements were attribution, consistent reporting and tools that connect activity to business outcomes.

## [Creator Partnerships Outside Crypto Make the Same Mistakes With Fewer Excuses.](https://lowob.com/research/creator-partnerships-fintech-ai/)

Published 2026-07-22. Web3 spent several years and a great deal of money learning what creator partnerships do and do not do: reach that produced nothing, screenshots instead of evidence, undisclosed payments, and audiences that turned out to be other creators. Fintech and AI companies now moving budget into the same channel can read those lessons, and regulators have turned several of them into rules. The FTC's 2024 rule bans buying fake followers and views, its Endorsement Guides make advertisers liable for deceptive endorsements, and the FCA holds firms responsible for financial promotions their influencers make. Creators are worth doing well, as a programme rather than a set of posts.

## [What Is Ad Fraud? Bots, MFA Sites, and Controls](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-ad-fraud/)

Published 2026-07-20. Ad fraud is any scheme that generates fake advertising activity (impressions, clicks, installs, views, leads) so that someone is paid for attention that never happened. It hides inside good-looking reports, because most of it is recorded as performance. How much a buyer loses depends on how it buys: TAG found invalid traffic under 1% in its certified US channels in 2024, while Juniper Research estimated 22% of all online ad spend was lost to fraud in 2023. Buy through inclusion lists with pre-bid verification, validate outcomes in your own systems, watch for numbers that are too clean, and use partners who are not paid more when volume rises.

## [Airdrops Can Buy Attention. They Cannot Buy Belief.](https://lowob.com/research/airdrops-points-community-incentives/)

Published 2026-07-19. Airdrops, points, ambassador programmes and referral rewards can overcome a cold start, but they also teach a community what the project values. The on-chain evidence on airdrops is consistent: Keyrock's review of 62 airdrops found most tokens fell within 15 days, and an academic study of nine major airdrops found up to 66% of claimed tokens moved to exchanges in the first transfer. Reward contribution quality and persistence, delay the largest rewards until value is observable, and count every incentive as acquisition cost.

## [Membership is the job](https://lowob.com/research/membership-is-the-job/)

Published 2026-07-17. A media audience is a list until it is a membership. Build the membership on sourcing, amplification and peer value, then measure it like a business line. The market makes the case: the Reuters Institute's 2026 Digital News Report found 17% of people across 20 paywall-heavy markets paid for online news, flat on the year, and reach of publishers' own sites and apps down 12 percentage points since 2021.

## [Brand Safety vs Brand Suitability: What They Cost You](https://lowob.com/research/brand-safety-and-suitability/)

Published 2026-07-15. Brand safety keeps a company's ads away from content that would harm it by association. Brand suitability keeps them near content that fits the brand and away from content that is legal and harmless but wrong for it. Both matter, and both are enforced by blunt tools that over-block by default: an analysis by Integral Ad Science and Reuters found a typical keyword blocklist would flag 54% of brand-suitable URLs in Reuters' news section. The industry's shared framework, GARM, was discontinued in August 2024. Set standards from actual risk, prefer category controls to keyword lists, allow reputable news and review what was blocked.

## [In Fintech, Trust Is the Product and the Channel Is Whoever Already Has It.](https://lowob.com/research/fintech-gtm-trust-distribution/)

Published 2026-07-14. A fintech product can offer a better price and a cleaner experience than an established competitor and still struggle to acquire customers, because people are being asked to trust an unfamiliar company with their money, identity or financial information. Paid channels add their own gate: Google now requires financial services advertisers to prove regulatory authorisation in a growing list of countries, with the US and Canada due in early 2027. The channels that work best are the people and platforms customers already trust, given approved facts to repeat and measured on funded, retained use rather than traffic.

## [What investors fund in media now](https://lowob.com/research/what-investors-fund-in-media-now/)

Published 2026-07-13. Investors fund media businesses with owned audiences that pay, proprietary products those audiences need, and revenue that does not depend on a platform. Reach is the raw material, not the asset. The 2026 data explains why: Google organic search traffic to more than 2,500 publisher sites fell 33% in a year, the share of people paying for online news held at about 17% across 20 countries, and media leaders expect AI licensing to be a minor contribution at best.

## [Ad Network vs Ad Exchange vs DSP: The Middlemen](https://lowob.com/research/ad-network-vs-exchange-vs-dsp/)

Published 2026-07-09. Ad networks bundle and resell publisher inventory with little visibility, ad exchanges run real-time auctions, and demand-side platforms (DSPs) are the software buyers use to bid. The DSP is where control lives. Audits show what is at stake: ISBA and PwC found UK publishers received 51% of advertiser spend in 2020, and the ANA found 29% of each US programmatic dollar went to transaction costs in 2023. Buyers should know which intermediary they are paying, what it charges and what it lets them see.

## [Founder-Led GTM Is Not a Vibe. It Is a Job With an Expiration Date.](https://lowob.com/research/founder-led-gtm-expiration-date/)

Published 2026-07-08. "Founder-led GTM" is often used as flattering shorthand for an early-stage company with a charismatic founder and no repeatable sales process. At the beginning, that can work. But founder-led GTM is a phase, not an identity. Its purpose is to discover and encode a commercial motion that other people can eventually operate. The research on start-up sales and founder succession points the same way: the skills that find the first customers are not the skills that scale the sale, and the transfer fails when the founder's judgment was never written down.

## [An audience is not a business](https://lowob.com/research/an-audience-is-not-a-business/)

Published 2026-07-06. An audience is an asset, not a business. A media business starts when you can say who the audience is, what it does, who pays for access to it, and which part of it you actually own. The market has made that test harder to dodge. The Reuters Institute's 2026 Digital News Report found that social and video platforms are now the most used route to online news, ahead of publishers' own sites and apps, and only 17% of people in 20 paywall-heavy markets paid for online news in the past year.

## [Native Advertising and Sponsored Content Explained](https://lowob.com/research/native-advertising-and-sponsored-content/)

Published 2026-07-06. Native advertising is paid placement designed to match the form and function of the content around it. Sponsored content is the subset where the advertiser supplies or commissions an actual piece, published by a third party with a paid label. Both exist because conventional ad formats are ignored, and both carry a risk conventional ads do not: being mistaken for editorial. In one University of Georgia study only 7% of readers identified a sponsored article as advertising. Disclosure is not optional, the advertiser is responsible alongside the publisher, and the format works best for products that need explaining.

## [Attribution vs Incrementality: What Did Your Marketing Actually Cause?](https://lowob.com/research/attribution-vs-incrementality/)

Published 2026-07-04. Attribution assigns credit for a conversion. Incrementality asks whether it would have happened without the campaign. Only the second answers the question a budget decision depends on, and it is answered by experiment, not by model. The research is blunt: in 15 Facebook experiments, observational methods using rich individual data were often off by a factor of three, and eBay found its brand search ads bought almost no traffic it would not have had anyway.

## [Claude Is Not Your Intern. Build a Repeatable GTM Workflow](https://lowob.com/research/claude-gtm-operating-system/)

Published 2026-07-01. Starting from a blank AI chat every day creates a lot of disconnected drafts. The better use is to give Claude maintained product facts, named commercial workflows and a clear human review rule. As documented in November 2026, Claude's Projects hold shared knowledge and instructions, Skills package repeatable procedures, and connectors reach company systems with per-tool approval settings. Those features make the model a context-aware operating layer. The durable advantage is the company-specific context and procedures, because competitors have the same model.

## [From funded account to lifetime value](https://lowob.com/research/from-funded-account-to-lifetime-value/)

Published 2026-06-30. Revenue in fintech is a chain from acquisition to lifetime value, and the two leaks that break it are accounts that never fund and accounts that fund once and go dormant. Losses are the third line most models leave out: LexisNexis Risk Solutions estimates that each dollar of fraud loss now costs US financial services firms $5.75 in total, up from $4.00 in 2021. Build the chain per channel, not blended, because channels that cost the same to acquire through can retain very differently.

## [What Is Connected TV Advertising? Should You Buy It?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-connected-tv-advertising/)

Published 2026-06-30. Connected TV (CTV) is television watched through an internet connection: streaming services, smart TV apps and devices plugged into a screen. Advertising on it is bought and measured like digital media, with audiences, frequency caps and reporting, while being seen like television, on a large screen with sound on. It is growing quickly: the IAB's 2026 Outlook forecast US CTV ad spend up 13.8%. It is best entered programmatically, measured by lift rather than clicks, and worth buying once a company has a working acquisition motion, a measurable brand constraint and confirmation that its category is permitted.

## [What Is Retargeting, and Why It Overclaims Credit](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-retargeting/)

Published 2026-06-25. Retargeting, also called remarketing, is advertising shown to people who have already visited a website, used an app or otherwise identified themselves to a company. It is cheap, it reports extraordinary results, and it is the channel most likely to be taking credit for customers who were coming anyway. Controlled experiments find its real effect is positive but modest: in one retailer's campaign, retargeting lifted purchases by about 11%, while an attribution report would have credited it with every purchase among the people it reached. Exclude converters, cap frequency, shorten windows, test with a holdout, and remember that email is retargeting you own.

## [One Channel Is Carrying You, and It Isn't Yours.](https://lowob.com/research/single-channel-dependency/)

Published 2026-06-24. The most dangerous distribution position is not being invisible. It is being visible on one channel that someone else controls. Platforms change rules, ranking systems and features on their own dates: Meta removed lookalike audiences for US financial ads in January 2025, Google cut low-quality results in search by 45% in 2024, and Pew found users clicked a result about half as often on Google searches that showed an AI summary. Price the dependency with three numbers, build a second channel with a different failure mode while the first one still pays for it, and keep no channel above half of outcomes for more than two quarters.

## [The people who vouch for you](https://lowob.com/research/the-people-who-vouch-for-you/)

Published 2026-06-24. In fintech, your community is the practitioners who advise your segment and the customers willing to be named. Give them a job, pay them openly where the rules allow, and measure referred funded accounts. The evidence that referrals are worth building is good: a study of about 10,000 customers at a German bank found referred customers were at least 16% more valuable over six years and less likely to leave. The rules are specific too. The FTC bans rewards conditioned on positive reviews, the FCA treats some practitioner posts as financial promotions, and in some products, such as US mortgage settlement services, paying for referrals is prohibited outright.

## [One Founder Interview Should Produce a Month of Content. Here Is the System.](https://lowob.com/research/founder-interview-content-engine/)

Published 2026-06-20. Most founder-content programs fail for one of two reasons: the founder is asked to become a full-time creator, or a marketing team imitates the founder without regular access to how the founder actually thinks. A better system treats the founder's time as a high-value source session. One focused interview records original thinking; a structured editorial workflow turns it into multiple useful assets without diluting the point of view. The payoff is credibility: in the 2024 Edelman-LinkedIn study, 73% of decision-makers said a firm's thought leadership was a more trustworthy basis for judging its capabilities than its marketing materials.

## [What SEO Is Now: How Search Ranking Works Today](https://lowob.com/research/what-seo-is-now/)

Published 2026-06-19. Modern SEO rewards pages that answer the query better than the alternatives, are technically sound and are trusted by other sites; it punishes volume and tricks. Search engines now answer many queries directly, and Ahrefs found an AI Overview correlated with a 58% lower click-through rate for the top result by late 2025. AI assistants are a parallel channel, and both reward clear early answers and checkable claims. Payback is slow, often slower than plans assume, but every company should do the minimum.

## [Distribute through whoever already holds the customer](https://lowob.com/research/distribute-through-whoever-already-holds-the-customer/)

Published 2026-06-17. Fintech cannot buy its way to customers. Trust moves through partners who already hold the relationship, practitioners who explain money, comparison and affiliate publishers, and the company's own channels. Paid advertising goes last and small: it is a reviewed category, approval can take weeks and be withdrawn, and search benchmarks show finance converting below average. The only measures that matter are cost per funded account and whether the account is still funded at 30, 90 and 365 days.

## [Email Deliverability Explained: SPF, DKIM, DMARC](https://lowob.com/research/email-deliverability-explained/)

Published 2026-06-16. Deliverability is whether your email reaches the inbox, and it rests on three layers: authentication, reputation, and content and behaviour. Since February 2024, Gmail and Yahoo have required bulk senders to authenticate with SPF, DKIM and DMARC, offer one-click unsubscribe and keep spam complaints below 0.3%. Outlook began rejecting non-compliant bulk mail in May 2025, and Gmail ramped up enforcement from November 2025. Set up the records once, warm the domain, send only to people who asked, clean the list and monitor the reports.

## [AI Companies Have a Distribution Problem Disguised as a Model Problem.](https://lowob.com/research/ai-companies-distribution-problem/)

Published 2026-06-15. A company can build an impressive AI product, show a great demo, and still struggle to find paying customers. Often the problem is not that the model needs another improvement. It is that the company has not worked out who needs the product, why they should trust it, or how they will discover it. The market evidence points the same way: enterprise AI spend reached about $177 billion in 2026 by Menlo Ventures' estimate, yet buyers increasingly say the models perform well enough, and they now judge AI products on security, cost, integration and proof.

## [Forget 10,000 Followers. Find Your First 100 People Who Actually Care.](https://lowob.com/research/first-100-community-members/)

Published 2026-06-12. The first meaningful community milestone is not 10,000 followers, 5,000 Discord members or a trending announcement. It is 100 people who understand why the project matters and repeatedly choose to participate. Our piece [The first hundred](https://lowob.com/research/the-first-hundred/) covers recruiting them; this one covers running them: what counts as caring, the one ritual to start with, the roles to give, the weekly review and when to grow.

## [How Marketing Teams Actually Use AI Tools](https://lowob.com/research/how-marketing-teams-use-ai/)

Published 2026-06-11. AI works best in marketing when it helps people read, organise, draft and check real work. The problem starts when teams mistake more output for more customer understanding. Surveys now show near-universal use: 88% of B2B marketers in the 2026 CMI and MarketingProfs survey said their organisation uses AI content tools. But 78% credited AI with speed and only 17% with quality, and 37% had no guidelines on when AI should not be used. The jobs that work are specific, repeatable and reviewed.

## [Raising in a regulated category](https://lowob.com/research/raising-in-a-regulated-category/)

Published 2026-06-11. Fintech investors underwrite trust and durability, not growth alone. Show the licence as an asset, the economics per funded account, the losses and the compliance cost in the model, and the plan for when a partner leaves. Two recent events sharpen every one of those questions: the 2024 bankruptcy of the banking-as-a-service provider Synapse, which led the FDIC to propose new recordkeeping rules for fintech custodial accounts, and a run of 2026 US charter approvals that gave some fintechs a path to holding the customer relationship themselves.

## [Performance Marketing Is Not a Channel. It Is a Way of Paying.](https://lowob.com/research/performance-marketing-way-of-paying/)

Published 2026-06-06. Performance marketing is a way of paying, not a channel. The company pays when something happens, an account opened, a subscription started, a qualified lead delivered, rather than when something is shown. It only works when three conditions hold: the outcome is observable in the company's own tracking, attributable with enough confidence to pay against, and worth the payment over a realistic horizon. If any of the three fails, the company is not paying for performance. It is paying for a story about performance.

## [What Is Conversion Rate Optimization, and When to Do It](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-conversion-rate-optimization/)

Published 2026-06-05. Conversion rate optimization (CRO) is the work of finding what stops suitable visitors from taking a useful action, changing it for a reason and checking whether the change helped. Much of the loss is friction rather than reluctance: Baymard Institute finds 70.22% of online carts are abandoned, and among the reasons shoppers give, unexpected extra costs lead at 40%. CRO needs the right success metric, enough traffic to test honestly, and visitors who were plausible buyers in the first place.

## [Trust is the product](https://lowob.com/research/trust-is-the-product/)

Published 2026-06-04. In fintech, trust is the product and the feature list is secondary. Trust is borrowed from institutions the buyer already trusts, proved in a fixed order, and every claim you make about money is compliance copy. The order matters more than it used to: the FDIC now treats a non-bank's failure to disclose that it is not a bank as a material omission, and the FCA reminds UK customers that funds held by payment and e-money firms are not directly protected by the FSCS. Lead with who holds the money. Put the yield second.

## [Landing Pages and Ad Review: Why Yours Gets Rejected](https://lowob.com/research/landing-pages-and-ad-review/)

Published 2026-06-02. A landing page does one job for one source and is reviewed by the ad platform before the visitor sees it. Reviewers check that the page matches the ad, works, identifies the business, carries the disclosures the category requires and makes no claims it cannot support; Google publishes most of these checks in its destination, misrepresentation and financial services policies. To pass and convert, match the ad, disclose the business, make compliant claims, answer the visitor's doubts, and never show reviewers and users different pages.

## [You Are Buying Media and You Do Not Trust the Numbers. You Are Right Not To.](https://lowob.com/research/programmatic-media-numbers-you-can-trust/)

Published 2026-06-02. The programmatic report arrives on the first of the month, and it is beautiful: impressions in the tens of millions, a CPM lower than last quarter's, a cost per click that seems too good. If you have wondered what any of that actually bought, you are not being paranoid. The ANA found that only 36 cents of each dollar entering a buying platform reached a consumer. The reporting layer of programmatic advertising was designed to be legible, not to be true. The fix is to report a different set of numbers: real CPM, verification pass rate and rejection rate.

## [Protocol revenue: what the protocol keeps and what to report](https://lowob.com/research/protocol-revenue-fees-real-yield-and-what-to-report/)

Published 2026-05-29. Report what the protocol keeps, with and without incentives, where it came from and what it cost to get. One page, monthly, same format every time. TVL is a balance, not revenue, and gross fees are not revenue either: protocol revenue is what is left after suppliers are paid. The evidence on incentives shows why the "without" column matters: after Arbitrum's airdrop, total fees rose while activity per address fell. And in the US, the SEC's 2026 offering proposal would ask issuers for exactly this kind of consistent economic disclosure.

## [Cold Outreach Works Better With a Real Reason to Talk](https://lowob.com/research/signal-based-outbound/)

Published 2026-05-28. Mentioning a prospect's podcast is not a reason to send a sales pitch. Better outreach starts with an observable change in the prospect's business and a problem you might solve because of it. Most buyers are not in market at any given time, and Gartner finds 67% would prefer to buy without a rep at all, so the bar for interrupting someone is high. Score each signal before you spend time on it, write from a hypothesis rather than a diagnosis, and use automation to cut research cost, not to raise send volume.

## [What Is Account-Based Marketing? A Small-Team Version](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-account-based-marketing/)

Published 2026-05-27. Account-based marketing (ABM) is a way of concentrating sales and marketing effort on a named set of companies that fit the product, rather than trying to reach everyone and hoping the right buyers respond. It fits sales of meaningful value that take time and involve several people; Forrester finds an average of 13 people involved in a B2B purchase. A small team can run it without a large platform: a short list, research on each account, one owner per account and measures that track account progress, not email volume.

## [Build an Affiliate Program Without Paying for Coupon Leaks](https://lowob.com/research/affiliate-program-asset-or-coupon-leak/)

Published 2026-05-25. Affiliate programs can introduce new customers, but weak commission rules also reward partners for sales that would have happened anyway. The most common leak is a coupon site or browser extension that appears at checkout, after the customer has decided, and collects the commission under last-click attribution. Google judged the practice serious enough to change its Chrome Web Store rules in 2025. The fix is in the terms: what is paid for, who qualifies, what is prohibited and how outcomes are validated, set before the program goes on a network.

## [Issuers, integrations and curators](https://lowob.com/research/issuers-integrations-and-curators/)

Published 2026-05-22. When paid channels are closed, distribution in crypto comes from the people who already have a reason to want you to succeed: issuers, integrations, curators and ecosystems. The closure is specific: Google bans ads for DeFi trading protocols, token liquidity pools and initial coin offerings in every market, and the UK bans refer-a-friend bonuses for crypto promotions. Work the list of people who gain when you grow before you spend a dollar on reach, and keep every piece of copy free of APYs and yield promises.

## [Product-Led vs Sales-Led vs Partner-Led Growth](https://lowob.com/research/product-led-vs-sales-led-vs-partner-led/)

Published 2026-05-22. Every company acquires customers through some combination of three motions: the product sells itself, people sell it, or other companies sell it. These are product-led, sales-led and partner-led growth. Most companies use more than one, but each needs a primary motion, because the three require different organizations. Choose the primary motion from how the buyer discovers, tries and buys the product, not from which one is cheapest, and add the others where they support it.

## [Community that survives the airdrop](https://lowob.com/research/community-that-survives-the-airdrop/)

Published 2026-05-18. Incentives buy activity, not community. Build for the people who stay when the payments stop, give them a job, and keep the record of who they are on channels you own. The on-chain record is consistent: two years after the Uniswap airdrop, Dune data showed 93% of recipients had sold all their UNI, and an academic study of nine airdrops found up to 66% of tokens were sold soon after claiming.

## [Audience vs Community: What Actually Makes the Difference?](https://lowob.com/research/community-vs-audience/)

Published 2026-05-18. A large follower count or Discord server is not automatically a community. The difference is whether people help, learn from and create value for one another. An audience receives. A customer transacts. A user engages with a product. A community member participates in a group whose value is partly created by other members. Each needs a different strategy, and the most common mistake is designing for one while measuring another.

## [What Is a Marketing Funnel, and When Does It Help?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-marketing-funnel/)

Published 2026-05-18. A marketing funnel is a model of the stages a stranger passes through before becoming a customer: awareness, consideration, evaluation, purchase and retention. It helps teams find where potential customers stop making progress. It is less useful as a map of how any individual buys, because research from Google and Gartner shows buyers loop back and skip stages. Use it to find the one stage that limits revenue now, and be wary of any plan described as "full-funnel".

## [How to Write an Ideal Customer Profile Sales Will Use](https://lowob.com/research/how-to-write-an-icp/)

Published 2026-05-13. An ideal customer profile, ICP, is a written description of the customer a company should pursue first: the one most likely to buy, most likely to succeed with the product, and most likely to stay. It should tell sales whom to pursue, why a company fits, and when to move on. A working ICP has five parts: firmographic facts, situational triggers, the buying committee, disqualifiers and the evidence it was built from. If every prospect qualifies, it is not an ICP.

## [A $10,000 Test That Closes a Question Beats a $10,000 Bet That Leaves It Open.](https://lowob.com/research/tests-that-close-questions/)

Published 2026-05-13. A test is defined by the decision it forces, not by its size. Write the question and the threshold first, measure several channels cheaply at once, then commit to one properly. The discipline matters because most ideas do not work: Kohavi and Thomke reported that only about a third of Microsoft's experiments improved the metric they targeted, and 10% to 20% at Google and Bing. A company that cannot say in advance what result would stop it will read most of its failures as "promising".

## [Token or no token](https://lowob.com/research/token-or-no-token/)

Published 2026-05-12. A token should reduce coordination cost or create ownership. If it does neither, do not issue one, and if you do, the type of money you raise decides your go-to-market before you write a line of it. Circulating float, the release schedule, stablecoin runway and liquidity depth say more than headline FDV. And in 2026 the US and EU both tie the legal treatment of a token to what the team says about it, so legal review is part of GTM, not a box ticked before it.

## [Percent of Spend Is a Conflict of Interest With a Logo on It.](https://lowob.com/research/percent-of-spend-media-fees/)

Published 2026-05-09. Most media agencies are still paid, in whole or part, as a percentage of what their clients spend. The agency's revenue goes up when spending goes up, not when spending works, so every recommendation about budget, channel or pace is made by a party paid more if the answer is "more." That is not an accusation of bad faith. It is a conflict of interest with a logo on it. The ANA's own research shows how the incentive plays out, and three rules remove it.

## [Positioning vs Messaging vs Branding: Which Is Broken?](https://lowob.com/research/positioning-vs-messaging-vs-branding/)

Published 2026-05-07. When marketing isn't connecting with buyers, a rebrand may be the wrong first fix. Positioning is the decision about what the company is, for whom and against what alternative. Messaging is the words that carry that decision. Branding is the system that makes the company recognizable and remembered between contacts. They are done in that order, and the cheapest test of which one is broken is to ask five people in the company to finish one sentence.

## [The user story before the token story](https://lowob.com/research/the-user-story-before-the-token-story/)

Published 2026-05-05. Write what the protocol does for a user in one sentence with no token in it. If you cannot, you have an instrument, not a product. Then give each audience one belief and one piece of evidence, and keep a claims register that survives both an audit and a narrative rotation: no yield numbers, no "safe", every audit named and dated. Regulators now read the same claims: MiCA requires marketing to be fair, clear, not misleading and consistent with the white paper, and the SEC's 2026 interpretation turns on what a team promised in public.

## [What Is a Distribution Diagnostic? One Week, Explained](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-distribution-diagnostic/)

Published 2026-05-04. A distribution diagnostic is a short, paid, scoped piece of work that answers which channels can carry a product to its buyer, what each costs, and where the next serious money should go. It has a fixed duration, price and written output, runs small real tests, and carries no obligation to continue. It differs from the free alternatives because someone pays for it: the European agency association found an average new-business pitch costs an agency about €43,800, and that cost is recovered in the engagement that follows. A week can show whether a channel is open and converts at all. It cannot replace the four to six weeks Google recommends for a controlled experiment.

## [AI Did Not Fix Your Marketing. It Made Your Mediocrity Cheaper.](https://lowob.com/research/ai-made-average-marketing-cheaper/)

Published 2026-05-03. The easiest thing to do with AI is produce more, and it is the least interesting. When every company has capable models, production speed stops being an advantage; the scarce inputs become judgment, access, evidence and a point of view. A 2024 Science Advances study found AI ideas made individual stories better but made the stories more similar to one another, and B2B marketers credit AI with speed (78%) far more than quality (17%). If the input is public consensus, the output will be polished consensus.

## [Thin Bidding: The Cheapest Attention Is Wherever Nobody Else Is Buying.](https://lowob.com/research/thin-bidding/)

Published 2026-04-30. Ask a media buyer why a click costs what it costs and you will hear about audiences, creative and relevance scores. All of that is true, and none of it is the first cause. The first cause is the number of companies bidding for the same person's attention at the same moment. Where the crowd is thick, attention is expensive; where it is thin, attention is cheap, whether or not anyone has noticed. WARC estimates Alphabet, Amazon and Meta took 56.1% of global ad spend outside China in 2025. Look where few look, and measure before you commit.

## [Brand vs Performance Marketing: Different Time Horizons](https://lowob.com/research/brand-vs-performance-marketing/)

Published 2026-04-29. Brand and performance marketing are not rivals; they work on different clocks. Performance buys measurable outcomes now. Brand makes future outcomes more likely and cheaper. The best-known evidence, Binet and Field's analysis of IPA effectiveness cases, puts the long-run optimum near 60% brand and 40% activation for consumer brands, and 46:54 in B2B. Most small companies cannot start there. They should fund performance first, then shift a growing share toward brand as revenue allows, measuring each on its own timescale.

## [Seats, usage or outcomes](https://lowob.com/research/seats-usage-or-outcomes/)

Published 2026-04-29. Pick the pricing model that matches how value shows up, know your cost per task, and report the eight numbers that show whether the business works. Seats fit when a named person uses the product daily; usage fits when value scales with volume; outcomes fit when both sides trust the measurement. Most AI companies now land on a hybrid: Kyle Poyar's 2026 survey of 230 software companies found 37% use one, up from 25% a year earlier. Whatever the model, a price set without a known cost per task is a guess.

## [Your Startup Needs a GTM Strategy, Not Just a List of Tactics](https://lowob.com/research/gtm-strategy-vs-tactics/)

Published 2026-04-25. A go-to-market plan connects the right buyer, a useful promise, a credible channel and measurable customer behavior. Most startup plans are lists of tactics instead: launch the site, hire a seller, post, sponsor, build a Discord. A tactic answers what the team will do. A strategy answers why these actions should create an advantage for this company, with this customer, at this moment. The test is coherence: four decisions on market, message, motion and measurement that reinforce one another.

## [How to Read a Media Plan Before You Approve It](https://lowob.com/research/how-to-read-a-media-plan/)

Published 2026-04-23. A media plan is the document that says where a marketing budget will be spent, over what period, in what proportions, and what each part is expected to produce. It is the point at which strategy turns into money, and it is usually approved by people who have not been told how to read one. Read three things first: the objective, the expected outcomes and the cost basis. Then check where programmatic money actually goes, since the ANA found the average campaign in its 2023 study ran on about 44,000 websites.

## [Raising for an AI company](https://lowob.com/research/raising-for-an-ai-company/)

Published 2026-04-22. Investors now price AI application companies on workflow ownership, margin and retention, so raise on that evidence and put the model in the appendix. The money is there: AI companies took 82.7% of US venture deal value through September 2026. But a large share went to a handful of model companies, and the application companies that raise well show what any software company shows, plus two numbers only AI companies carry: gross margin after inference, and what happens when the model provider ships their feature.

## [Meta Said No. That Is Not the End of Your Distribution Plan.](https://lowob.com/research/distribution-when-ad-platforms-restrict-you/)

Published 2026-04-21. A rejected ad account is the first distribution decision made on your behalf, and it is made by a reviewer who never sees the product. Treat the ad platforms as one band of channels among three, not as the plan. Sort every channel into open, restricted or closed for each geography, build first in the open band, and file the restricted-band paperwork with nothing forecast against it. The rules move often: Google added verification for financial advertisers in 24 European markets in June 2026, and Meta made a special ad category mandatory for US financial ads in January 2025.

## [How Marketing Services Are Priced: Five Fee Models](https://lowob.com/research/how-marketing-services-are-priced/)

Published 2026-04-20. Marketing services are priced five ways: retainer, project fee, hourly or daily, percent of spend, and performance. Each rewards the provider for something different, so find what makes the fee go up and you have found the advice you will get. The market is moving: a 2026 study of 69 multinational advertisers found fewer than a fifth now pay agencies mainly for time, and 61% plan to change their commercial models because of AI. Yet only 45% said they had enough visibility into how agencies cost and profit from the work.

## [Developers, marketplaces and the answer engines](https://lowob.com/research/developers-marketplaces-and-the-answer-engines/)

Published 2026-04-16. AI distribution runs through the platforms you plug into, the assistants buyers ask, and the people who build on you. Pick one lead motion, layer the compounding channels, and spend on paid last. The evidence for each channel is now concrete: 45% of B2B buyers in Gartner's 2026 survey had used generative AI during a purchase, cloud marketplaces let buyers spend committed cloud budgets on your product, and product-led adoption carried 27% of AI application spend in Menlo Ventures' 2025 survey.

## [What Is a Restricted Category in Advertising?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-restricted-category/)

Published 2026-04-14. A restricted category is a group of products an ad platform will advertise only with conditions, such as prior approval, proof of licensing, certification, geographic limits, age limits or required disclaimers. Platforms sort every product into prohibited, restricted or open, using a process built to prefer refusing a legitimate business over approving a harmful one. Financial services, crypto, health, gambling and alcohol are restricted on most platforms, with rules that differ by country and change several times a year. Treat the classification as a map of where to build, not as a review to argue with.

## [The pilot that survives security review](https://lowob.com/research/the-pilot-that-survives-security-review/)

Published 2026-04-09. AI pilots die from security review, missing owners, demo-grade accuracy and pricing confusion. Design the pilot to pass all four before you sign it. Gartner predicted that at least 30% of generative AI projects would be abandoned after proof of concept by the end of 2025, citing poor data quality, inadequate risk controls, escalating costs and unclear business value. Those are pilot design failures, and most of them can be closed before the first call.

## [What Go-to-Market Means: A Plain Guide for Founders](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-gtm-for-founders/)

Published 2026-04-09. Go-to-market, GTM, is the plan for how a company will find its customers, convince them to buy, and do so at a cost that leaves a business. It is bigger than a launch calendar. It is four decisions: who exactly, what they must believe, how trust moves, and what evidence proves it is working. A company has a GTM when it can write one sentence for each of the four and the four sentences agree with each other.

## [How Marketing Tracking Works: Pixels to Server-Side](https://lowob.com/research/how-marketing-tracking-works/)

Published 2026-04-03. Every marketing number depends on tracking: connecting a person who saw or clicked something with a person who later did something. Pixels see less every year, because Safari blocks third-party cookies by default, Apple requires permission before apps track users, and consent rules cover much of the rest. Platforms fill the gaps with modelled estimates. First-party data, server-side tracking, tagged links and consent are the measurement layer that survives, and the company should own it, not whoever runs its media.

## [The model is not the product](https://lowob.com/research/the-model-is-not-the-product/)

Published 2026-04-03. Buyers do not pay for a model. They pay for a finished job. Position on the job, prove every AI claim, and tell investors a different story from customers. The market has made this sharper: 37% of enterprises in a16z's 2025 CIO survey used five or more models, and model market share swings by double digits in a year, so a pitch built on the model is a pitch any competitor can copy.

## [CPM, CPC, CPA, CPL, ROAS Explained: Which to Run On](https://lowob.com/research/cpm-cpc-cpa-cpl-roas-explained/)

Published 2026-03-31. CPM, CPC, CPL and CPA describe what a company pays for, and each one hides what the next reveals. ROAS flatters: Google's own definition divides conversion value by ad spend and nothing else, so margin, fees and the attribution model all sit outside it. The number to manage the business on is customer acquisition cost (CAC) against value over a realistic horizon, with payback period as the constraint.

## [Build it to run without you](https://lowob.com/research/build-it-to-run-without-you/)

Published 2026-03-27. A GTM system is only an asset if the company owns it: the accounts, the records, the routines and the reasons. Most firms lose the last two first. A Panopto survey estimated 42% of institutional knowledge is unique to the individual in the role, so it leaves when they do. Build for handover from day one, write handover into any outside scope, then score yourself across all ten parts of this series and fix the weakest link first.

## [Influencer vs Creator vs KOL vs Ambassador: Definitions](https://lowob.com/research/influencer-creator-kol-ambassador/)

Published 2026-03-25. Influencers sell reach, creators sell content and conversion, KOLs sell authority in a specific domain, and ambassadors sell an ongoing, disclosed relationship. The people may overlap, but the deals should not. Pay each for what they sell, disclose every material connection, and run the whole as a program. The spend is large enough to deserve the discipline: the IAB put US creator ad spend at $37 billion in 2025, growing about four times faster than the media industry as a whole.

## [Stop reporting reach](https://lowob.com/research/stop-reporting-reach/)

Published 2026-03-23. Pick the few numbers that show attention turning into money that comes back: activation, retention, revenue, efficiency and source. Instrument them before you spend on growth, report them to everyone who matters, and drop the vanity metrics from the top of the page. Reach is the easiest number to grow and the weakest evidence: a display impression counts as viewable when half the ad is on screen for one second, and in Keyrock's study of 62 airdrops in 2024, 88% of tokens lost value, most within 15 days.

## [Affiliate vs Partner vs Referral Programs: What's the Difference?](https://lowob.com/research/affiliate-vs-partner-vs-referral/)

Published 2026-03-20. Affiliate, partner and referral programs all pay other people to bring a company customers, but each needs different incentives and different measures. Affiliate programs pay professional publishers a commission per defined event, at scale; US affiliate investment was about $13.6 billion in 2024. Partner programs are fewer, larger deals negotiated between companies. Referral schemes give existing customers small rewards for bringing people they know, and the best study of them, at a bank, found referred customers were worth at least 16% more. Which one a company needs depends on who could plausibly send it a customer.

## [Distribution when the platforms are closed](https://lowob.com/research/distribution-when-the-platforms-are-closed/)

Published 2026-03-17. Rank channels by the cost of earning a buyer's attention, and start where the attention is cheapest and the trust is borrowed: partners, referrals, creators and owned media. Paid media comes last, once you know what converts. Before any of that, sort every channel into open, restricted or closed for your category and geography, using the platforms' own published policies with the date you checked them.

## [How AI Answer Engines Choose Which Sources to Cite](https://lowob.com/research/how-llms-choose-sources/)

Published 2026-03-17. AI answer engines draw on two things: what the model learned in training, and pages a search system retrieves when the question is asked. The retrieved sources vary by engine, by question and by day. Ahrefs found half or more of the citations in five AI tools had gone by the next day's answer, and only about 12% of URLs cited by ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot ranked in Google's top 10 for the same prompt. No single trick guarantees a citation. The best starting point is useful, specific, verifiable information that a crawler can reach.

## [LLM Optimization Checklist for Content and Marketing](https://lowob.com/research/llm-optimization-checklist/)

Published 2026-03-11. If customers ask AI assistants about your category, your site should be easy to find, accurate, accessible and worth citing. That means one real question answered per page, claims a reader can check, crawlable HTML, genuine references on sites you do not own, and a monthly measurement routine. Google's July 2026 guidance says no llms.txt file, special schema or content chunking is needed for its AI features. The one controlled study of generated answers found quotations, statistics and cited sources raised a page's visibility, and keyword stuffing lowered it.

## [Your first ten customers are design partners](https://lowob.com/research/your-first-ten-customers-are-design-partners/)

Published 2026-03-10. Pick early customers for fit and learning, not logo value. Agree a written success test up front, work closely for six to twelve weeks, and convert the ones that succeed into paying customers, case studies and references. The evidence favours this: CB Insights found 42% of 101 startup post-mortems cited no market need, and RAND's 2024 study of AI projects found that unclear problems, unclear success metrics and missing data were among the main reasons more than 80% of them fail.

## [Paid, Earned, Shared, Owned Media Explained](https://lowob.com/research/paid-earned-shared-owned-media/)

Published 2026-03-06. Every channel a company can use to reach people falls into one of four kinds of media. Paid is bought, earned is given, shared is borrowed, owned is kept. The model, popularised as PESO by Gini Dietrich of Spin Sucks, is useful because it shows where control and cost sit. Research explains why each does a different job: Nielsen found recommendations from people we know are the most trusted source, and a meta-analysis found publicity outperforms advertising for unfamiliar products. A working system routes attention from the first three toward the owned layer.

## [The first hundred](https://lowob.com/research/the-first-hundred/)

Published 2026-03-04. The first hundred community members are recruited, not attracted. Hand-pick them, give them real influence and close the loop on every contribution. They become your testers, your references and your first distribution channel. This piece is about getting them: who to list, what to ask and how 30 names become 100. Its companion, [Find your first 100 people who actually care](https://lowob.com/research/first-100-community-members/), covers what to do once they are in the room.

## [What Is a Press Release, and When Is It Worth It?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-press-release/)

Published 2026-03-02. A press release is a short, formal announcement a company issues to the media, and increasingly to the public directly, about something it wants known. It is a canonical record of the facts, not a marketing channel and not coverage. Journalists still rely on PR material, but Cision's 2026 survey of 1,899 journalists found only 22% wanted more press releases, against 47% wanting data or research, and 82% rejected pitches for being irrelevant. Issue a release when the news is material and citable, write it plainly, and do the pitching separately.

## [Community is a job, not a number](https://lowob.com/research/community-is-a-job-not-a-number/)

Published 2026-02-25. A community earns its keep by doing work the company would otherwise pay for. Decide the job first, design the community around it, and measure contribution instead of size. Member count is the most common health measure in the field, used by 84% of community teams in CMX's 2025 survey, and it is also the easiest number to inflate and the hardest for anyone outside to verify.

## [What an Advisor Does for a Web3 Company](https://lowob.com/research/what-advisors-do-web3-companies/)

Published 2026-02-25. A useful Web3 advisor helps founders make a small number of consequential, often irreversible decisions well: which audience moves first, how much to spend on incentives, which decisions need counsel, where distribution exists beyond the crypto timeline, what institutions need, and when to say "you are not ready". The structure matters as much as the advice. US and EU rules treat undisclosed paid promotion and public promises as legal facts, so put the scope in writing, lock the tokens and disclose every connection.

## [Run the round like a sales process](https://lowob.com/research/run-the-round-like-a-sales-process/)

Published 2026-02-19. Treat investors as accounts. Pick them for fit, research each one, get in warm, run the process in a tight window, and track every firm through stages the way a sales team tracks a pipeline. Fit now includes a question many founders skip: whether the fund still has money to invest. In 2026, managers on their fourth fund or later captured 88.2% of US venture fundraising dollars through September, and first-time funds closed at a decade-low pace.

## [What an Advisor Does for an AI Company](https://lowob.com/research/what-advisors-do-ai-companies/)

Published 2026-02-19. An advisor helps an AI company decide, introduces it to the people who matter, and tells it which advantages will not last. Scope the relationship in writing, vest the equity, and hire separately for anything that is a job. The market benchmarks are modest: Carta's data puts median pre-seed advisor equity well under 0.25%, typically vesting over two years with a short cliff, and the Founder Institute's standard template ranges from 0.15% to 1% depending on stage and commitment.

## [Self-Serve vs Managed Desk vs Agency: Who Runs Your Media?](https://lowob.com/research/self-serve-vs-managed-media/)

Published 2026-02-16. Self-serve suits small budgets in categories the platforms welcome, provided someone refuses the defaults, which are designed around the platform's revenue. A flat-fee managed desk suits budgets past the fee floor, restricted categories and channels beyond the self-serve platforms. An agency suits large, multi-channel spend where buying power and planning matter more than fee structure. Whatever you choose, the ad accounts, conversion tracking, pixel history and analytics stay in your company's name.

## [Raise against evidence, not narrative](https://lowob.com/research/raise-against-evidence-not-narrative/)

Published 2026-02-12. Investors price risk. Narrative asks them to imagine the risk away; evidence removes some of it. Even a small amount of real evidence changes which investors take the call, how fast they move and what they ask for. That matters more in 2026 than it did two years ago, because venture money is concentrating: rounds of $100 million or more took 87.5% of US venture dollars in the first half of the year, and seed capital on Carta's platform fell by almost half.

## [What Is Programmatic Advertising? A Plain-English Guide](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-programmatic-advertising/)

Published 2026-02-10. Programmatic advertising is the buying and selling of ad space by software, through auctions that take place in the time it takes a page to load. That sentence covers most of what a buyer needs to know. The rest is vocabulary, and the vocabulary is where the money hides: the Association of National Advertisers (ANA) found in 2023 that only 36 cents of each dollar entering a buying platform reached a consumer. Programmatic is useful, but only to buyers who set standards before they spend.

## [One truth, three audiences](https://lowob.com/research/one-truth-three-audiences/)

Published 2026-02-06. Write one product truth, then one belief statement per audience, then a claims register that says what you can prove. Everything else (the deck, the homepage, the community announcements) is derived from those three. The product truth is one sentence: what it is, who buys it, and what changed that makes it necessary now. The claims register is a short table of every public claim with its evidence and approver; regulators in the US and UK already expect that evidence to exist before the claim is made.

## [Agency Types Explained: Full-Service to Specialist](https://lowob.com/research/agency-types-field-guide/)

Published 2026-02-05. Agencies specialise, and the specialisation determines what you get. The main types are full-service, performance, media, creative, PR and specialist agencies, each paid differently and good at different things. The buying pattern of large advertisers points the same way: in the ANA's 2023 survey, 82% of members had an in-house agency and 92% still used outside agencies, mainly for capacity or skills they lacked. Most small and mid-sized companies need one partner who owns distribution and brings in specialists, not a full-service agency.

## [Agency vs Consultancy vs Advisor vs Fractional: Explained](https://lowob.com/research/agency-vs-consultancy-vs-advisor/)

Published 2026-02-02. Agencies sell execution, consultancies sell answers, advisors sell judgment over time, and fractional executives sell part-time ownership of a function. Each is paid differently, and the payment tells you what you are really buying. The four markets are shifting at once: Lightcast counts at least 34,000 US workers with "fractional" in their title, up 265% since 2019, and Gartner found 22% of CMOs say generative AI has reduced their reliance on agencies for creativity and strategy. Match the purchase to what you are missing, and insist on a paid, scoped first step from anyone offering more than one.

## [You don't have three problems](https://lowob.com/research/you-dont-have-three-problems/)

Published 2026-02-02. Fundraising, community and customer acquisition are three outputs of one commercial system. Teams that run them as separate projects pay for the same work three times and still end up with a story nobody believes. The three depend on each other in a fixed order: a named buyer, early evidence from that buyer, a community that produces more of that evidence cheaply, and a round that funds distribution. In 2026 the order matters more, because capital is concentrating and investors are spending their limited reading time on traction.
